body:
## Background

The current capstones prove finite-horizon existence with the quantifier order

```text
∀ T > 0, ∃ u_T,  u_T is a Leray–Hopf weak solution on [0,T].
```

This is mathematically standard and is documented accurately in `docs/claims-and-scope.md`. It is not, however, the literal single-trajectory statement

```text
∃ u, ∀ T > 0,  u restricted to [0,T] is a Leray–Hopf weak solution on [0,T].
```

Because weak solutions are not known to be unique, the latter does not follow by choosing arbitrary finite-horizon witnesses and gluing them. The standard route is to start from one forward-global Galerkin approximation sequence, extract nested subsequences on `[0,1]`, `[0,2]`, …, and take a diagonal subsequence whose limit is valid on every finite interval.

This is a genuine post-release extension, not a soundness defect in the current capstones or in `v0.1.0-rc1`.

## Why this is nontrivial in the current Lean architecture

The mathematical argument is standard, but the present API exposes two formalization costs.

### 1. The Galerkin sequence is index-dependent

The approximation family has the shape

```lean
∀ n, GalerkinSolutionData F ν u₀ n
```

After extracting `φ : ℕ → ℕ`, the reindexed family has type

```lean
∀ k, GalerkinSolutionData F ν u₀ (φ k)
```

and cannot be passed directly to fixed-horizon builders that expect index `k` itself. The compactness layer likely needs to be generalized to an increasing mode map `κ : ℕ → ℕ`, with subsequent extraction represented by composition `κ ∘ φ`, or refactored to consume an index-independent package of curves and uniform estimates.

### 2. The global representative must be coherent pointwise

Finite-horizon `L²(0,T;L²)` limits give overlap agreement only almost everywhere unless additional structure is used. The current construction also carries pointwise weak convergence against test vectors internally. A robust globalization should use a common diagonal subsequence and uniqueness of weak limits in the ambient Hilbert space to obtain a single curve `u : Time → σ` whose restrictions agree with the finite-horizon limits.

## Proposed scope

This issue is initially a **design and feasibility task**, not a commitment to implement both domains immediately.

The first target should be the torus lane, where the mode-wise compactness construction and its extracted subsequence are already explicit. The ℝ³ lane should follow only after the abstraction is validated.

## Proposed work plan

1. Prove a PDE-independent diagonal-subsequence lemma for a nested family of strictly monotone extraction maps.
2. Generalize the fixed-horizon compactness API to work over an arbitrary strictly increasing Galerkin mode map, or design an equivalent index-independent abstraction.
3. Build a torus-only spike showing that one diagonal subsequence converges on every interval `[0,m]`.
4. Prove coherence of the finite-horizon limit curves on overlaps, preferably through the existing pointwise weak-convergence information rather than only `L²` a.e. equality.
5. Define a global solution contract, for example a structure containing one curve `u : Time → σ` together with proofs that every positive finite horizon satisfies the present finite-horizon Leray–Hopf contract.
6. Prove a torus global capstone.
7. Assess which abstractions transfer unchanged to the ℝ³ lane before opening an implementation issue for that lane.

## Suggested global contract

The exact API is part of the design task, but the intended logical content is:

```lean
structure GlobalLerayHopfSolution (...) where
  u : Time → σ
  finite_horizon : ∀ T : ℝ, 0 < T →
    LerayHopfSolution ... T u₀
```

The actual structure should avoid duplicating the curve inside each finite-horizon witness; restriction/coherence should be explicit in the type.

## Acceptance criteria for this design issue

- [ ] A precise mathematical proof outline is written for the torus lane, including the nested-subsequence and overlap-coherence arguments.
- [ ] The index-dependent `GalerkinSolutionData ... n` obstacle is resolved at the API-design level.
- [ ] A minimal Lean spike proves the required abstract diagonal-subsequence lemma.
- [ ] A minimal Lean spike demonstrates that the generalized compactness interface can be instantiated with a previously extracted subsequence.
- [ ] The proposed global solution structure states `∃ u, ∀ T > 0` literally and does not merely repackage `∀ T > 0, ∃ u_T`.
- [ ] The implementation cost and likely reuse for the ℝ³ lane are reassessed before opening full implementation sub-issues.

## Non-goals

- Treating the current finite-horizon capstones as incorrect.
- Changing the claims of `v0.1.0-rc1`.
- Assuming uniqueness of weak solutions.
- Gluing arbitrarily chosen finite-horizon witnesses.
- Re-proving Aubin–Lions or introducing new Navier–Stokes estimates.
- Implementing both the torus and ℝ³ global capstones in this initial issue.

## Priority

**P2 / post-release.** The mathematical result is worthwhile and closes the quantifier-order gap between arbitrary finite horizons and a literal single global trajectory. The expected implementation cost is substantial relative to the incremental theorem-strengthening, so this should proceed only after the design spike confirms that the required API generalization is contained.
title: [P2][math][design] Global-in-time Leray–Hopf solution via diagonal extraction

body:
## Summary

Closes #191. Adds a static, standalone SVG treemap visualizing per-file **code LOC** (physical lines minus blank and comment lines) across `LerayHopf.lean` / `LerayHopf/**/*.lean`, and features it as a "Repository map" in the README with the full write-up in `docs/architecture.md`.

## What was built

- **Measurement**: `cloc --by-file --json --quiet LerayHopf.lean LerayHopf`, run from the repo root. `cloc` is pulled in as a pinned devDependency (`cloc@2.6.0-cloc`, the official AlDanial/cloc release published to npm) of the isolated tool directory — no hand-rolled Lean lexer.
- **Treemap**: `d3-hierarchy@3.1.2`'s `treemapSquarify`. Directories (`Analysis/`, `Bochner/`, `Galerkin/`, `R3/`, `Torus/`) are internal nodes; Lean files are leaves. `LerayHopf.lean` and the files directly under `LerayHopf/` (e.g. `Core.lean`) are root-level leaves per the issue's spec. Leaf area is proportional to `code` LOC only (comment/blank are recorded but never affect area). Color is assigned per top-level module (Okabe–Ito colorblind-safe palette), deterministic and consistent across the same directory.
- **Labels**: file name + `NNN LOC` only on rectangles with enough area (69 of 97 files at the chosen canvas size); every leaf has an SVG `<title>` with full path, code, comment, and blank counts.
- **Output**: `docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.svg` (standalone, `viewBox`, no `<script>`, no external fonts/remote assets — verified with `grep`) + `docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.json` (per-file `{path, code, comment, blank}`, cloc version, generating commit).
- **Tooling isolation**: `tools/code-treemap/` has its own `package.json` + `package-lock.json` (`d3-hierarchy` dependency, `cloc` devDependency), fully separate from the Lake package. `node_modules/` and the intermediate `build/` are gitignored.

## Regeneration command

```bash
cd tools/code-treemap
npm install   # installs pinned cloc + d3-hierarchy, isolated from the Lake package
npm run build # -> ../../docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.svg and .json
```

(`npm run build` = `npm run measure` (`cloc --by-file --json --quiet LerayHopf.lean LerayHopf` from repo root, via the pinned local `cloc` binary) + `npm run generate` (`node tools/code-treemap/generate-code-loc-treemap.mjs`).)

## Determinism check

Ran the full `npm run build` twice from a clean state and compared `sha256sum` of the outputs:

```
8c787c4ab8e019f9206cc546c307905965911add31e6cde3eccadf243da5cb8a  docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.svg   (run 1 == run 2)
6e542d6042101cbf1ab335041a1f3f210e68a7d589b82378c9f7ec866ce7ba60  docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.json  (run 1 == run 2)
```

Both files were **byte-identical** across the two runs. (The intermediate `build/code-loc.json` — cloc's raw output — differs run-to-run because cloc embeds non-deterministic timing stats, `elapsed_seconds`/`files_per_second`, in its header; the generator only reads `header.cloc_version` from that file and ignores the timing fields, so this never reaches the final SVG/JSON.) No `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` is used anywhere in the generator; the only "commit" reference embedded in the SVG metadata is `git rev-parse HEAD`, i.e. derived from repository state, not wall-clock time.

## Placement

- **README.md**: new `## Repository map` section, placed after "Getting started" and before "Documentation, contributing, citation, license" — below the main-results and interactive-notes links, per the issue's constraint. Caption states area = code LOC and that the figure is not a proxy for proof difficulty/importance/quality.
- **docs/architecture.md**: new `## Visual overview: code LOC treemap` section at the top (before the module-map prose), with the full-size figure, an expanded caption, the regeneration command, and a note on what the metadata records.

## Non-goals confirmed untouched

No Lean source, theorem statement, CI workflow, or release-attestation file was modified — this PR touches only `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/assets/*`, and the new `tools/code-treemap/` directory. No `lake build` was run.

## Test plan

- [x] `cloc --by-file --json` correctly measures all 97 files under `LerayHopf.lean`/`LerayHopf/**/*.lean` (verified count and total: 97 files, 25,451 code LOC)
- [x] Generated SVG parses as valid XML (`xml.etree.ElementTree`)
- [x] No `<script>` tags, no remote `http(s)://` asset/font references (only the `xmlns` namespace URI and internal `url(#clip-...)` references)
- [x] Two independent `npm run build` runs produce byte-identical SVG/JSON (sha256 above)
- [x] README and architecture.md render correctly with the embedded SVG (spot-checked markdown)
- [x] `git -C /workspaces/lean-pde push` pre-push gate passed with "no Lean/build changes — skipping build"

title: docs: add deterministic code-LOC treemap as repository map

Query-parameter separators are HTML-entity-escaped (`&`) for valid markup; the decoded URL and sealed token are unchanged. - Placed **below** the overview, Main results, Verification status, and Getting started sections, and **above** Documentation/contributing/citation/license — so it does not visually compete with the mathematical content or the interactive-notes link (issue #189's placement requirement). - No explanatory caption in the README: per owner review on this PR, the "stars are a visibility signal, not a quality/correctness proxy" framing from the issue is intentionally **not** included in the README body — the owner judged it unnecessary and asked for the section to stay minimal (heading + chart only). - Added a maintainer runbook section to `docs/build-and-checks.md` ("README Star History embed (issue #189)") documenting: what the sealed-token embed is (fine-grained PAT, repo-scoped, read-only; sealed token is Star History's public-safe embed value, not the raw PAT), and the steps to regenerate/rotate it if it expires or breaks (Star History's authenticated-embed guide, replace the `sealed_token` in all three URLs, re-verify with a concrete anonymous curl check using raw `&` separators — not the README's `&` — or remove the embed if Star History is down for an extended period). ## Verification - **Embed source:** copied verbatim from `t-uda`'s comment on #189 — no token was retyped or regenerated. `sealed_token=seblTJCpa7k-Ww...` appears exactly 3 times in `README.md` (dark ``, light ``, `` fallback), matching the owner's block byte-for-byte (modulo the `&`→`&` HTML entity escaping requested in review). - **Anonymous render check** (issue #189 acceptance criterion — unauthenticated viewers must see the chart), re-run after the `&` escaping change: ``` curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type} %{size_download}' \ "https://api.star-history.com/chart?repos=uda-lab/leray-hopf&type=date&legend=top-left&sealed_token=..." → 200 image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8 64479 ``` Plain `curl`, no auth headers/cookies — confirms the chart is publicly viewable. - **No raw PAT committed:** `grep -rEni "ghp_|github_pat_|gho_|(ACTIONS?_|SECRET|password)="` over the changed files returns nothing. Only the sealed embed URL (Star History's public-safe value) is present, per the issue's security requirement. - **Token rotation note location:** `docs/build-and-checks.md` (new "README Star History embed (issue #189)" section at the end of the file), referenced from the README's Documentation list — not in the README body itself, keeping token mechanics out of the public-facing page. The runbook's curl snippet is a concrete URL (token placeholder only) with an explicit note to use raw `&`, not the README's `&`. - Docs-only change: no Lean source, theorem statements, CI config, or release-attestation workflow touched. `scripts/hooks/pre-push` guard ran clean (no Lean/build changes, so no `lake build` triggered). ## Test plan - [x] Star History embed matches the owner's #189 comment verbatim (token count matches, no retyping; `&`-escaped per review) - [x] Anonymous curl to the chart URL returns HTTP 200 with `image/svg+xml` content - [x] No raw token/secret pattern found in the diff - [x] Section placed below main results / verification status / getting started (does not precede them) - [x] No explanatory caption in the README (owner directive on this PR overrides the issue's suggested framing) - [x] Token-rotation runbook recorded in `docs/build-and-checks.md` for maintainers, with a concrete/runnable curl example - [x] Reviewer sign-off (owner + copilot review rounds addressed, all threads resolved) Refs #189

body:
## 背景

`leray-hopf` の Lean source は，3次元トーラス，全空間 `ℝ³`，Bochner 積分・時間発展，Galerkin 法，共通の関数解析基盤など，多数の module から構成されている．

現在の `docs/architecture.md` は依存関係と責務を文章で説明しているが，各 directory・file が source 全体の中でどの程度の規模を占めるかは視覚的に把握しにくい．

そこで，各 Lean file のコメント・空行を除いた code lines を面積に対応させ，directory 階層を長方形の入れ子として表す treemap を生成する．repository の数学的・実装上の構成を直感的に把握するための補助図として，README または architecture documentation に掲載する．

## 目的

- `LerayHopf/` 以下の Lean code の規模を file 単位で計測する
- directory 階層を保った D3 treemap を生成する
- 各 file の面積をコメント・空行を除いた code LOC に比例させる
- reproducible な静的 SVG として repository に保存する
- source tree の構成を一般読者にも視覚的に伝える

本図はコード品質，証明難度，数学的重要性を表すものではない．あくまで物理的な source code 規模の可視化とする．

## 対象

原則として次を対象とする．

```text
LerayHopf.lean
LerayHopf/**/*.lean
```

次は対象外とする．

- `.lake/`
- dependency source
- generated files
- scripts
- documentation
- tests または一時的な scratch files
- archive files

root module `LerayHopf.lean` は，treemap 上で root-level file として扱う．

## 計測値

面積には **code LOC** を用いる．ここで code LOC は，物理行数から空行とコメント行を除いた値とする．

初版では `cloc --by-file --json` 等の既存ツールを使用し，独自の Lean lexer や token counter は実装しない．

各 file について少なくとも次を中間データへ保存する．

```json
{
  "path": "LerayHopf/R3/Example.lean",
  "code": 420,
  "comment": 130,
  "blank": 58
}
```

treemap の面積には `code` だけを使用する．コメント率や blank 行数を面積・色へ混在させない．

## 可視化方式

D3 の hierarchy / treemap implementation を用い，directory を内部 node，Lean file を leaf node とする．

初版では `treemapSquarify` を使用し，縦横比が極端になり過ぎない長方形分割を生成する．

### 面積

各 leaf rectangle の面積を，その file の code LOC に比例させる．

### 色

色は code LOC とは別の意味に使い，最上位の module 群を区別する．例えば次を基準とする．

- `Torus/`
- `R3/`
- `Bochner/`
- root-level shared modules
- その他

色は directory ごとに決定し，同じ入力に対して常に同じ色になるようにする．file ごとのランダム色は使用しない．

### ラベル

十分な面積のある rectangle にだけ file name と code LOC を表示する．

例：

```text
GalerkinODECapstone.lean
812 LOC
```

小さ過ぎる rectangle には無理に文字を描画しない．各 leaf には SVG の `<title>` を付け，hover 時に少なくとも次を確認できるようにする．

- full path
- code LOC
- comment lines
- blank lines

初版では file ごとの hyperlink や interactive navigation は実装しない．

## 出力

候補：

```text
docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.svg
docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.json
scripts/generate-code-loc-treemap.mjs
tools/code-treemap/package.json
tools/code-treemap/package-lock.json
```

実際の配置は既存の repository 構成に合わせて調整してよい．

SVG は次を満たすこと．

- standalone SVG として直接閲覧できる
- `viewBox` を持ち，README 上で縮小表示できる
- JavaScript を含まない静的 SVG
- external font や remote asset に依存しない
- deterministic に再生成できる
- file path，計測方法，生成 commit を metadata または注記として残す

## 生成手順

一つの command または短い二段階 command で再生成できるようにする．

例：

```bash
cloc --by-file --json LerayHopf.lean LerayHopf/ > build/code-loc.json
node scripts/generate-code-loc-treemap.mjs \
  build/code-loc.json \
  docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.svg
```

実装時には，引数，必要な dependency，生成先を一つの documented command に固定する．

Node dependency は root の Lean build から分離し，treemap generator 専用の小さな tool directory に閉じ込める．version は lockfile で固定する．

## README / documentation への掲載

README の main results や interactive notes への導線より上には置かない．

候補：

```markdown
## Repository map

The area of each rectangle is proportional to the number of non-comment,
non-blank lines in the corresponding Lean source file.

![Lean source code treemap](docs/assets/code-loc-treemap.svg)
```

README が過密になる場合は，`docs/architecture.md` に大きく掲載し，README には縮小画像または短いリンクだけを置く．

#188 / PR #190 の一般読者向け README 構成を損なわない位置を選ぶ．

## 更新方針

初版では自動 schedule や毎 commit の regeneration は導入しない．

次のいずれかで手動更新する．

- 大規模な module 分割・統合を行ったとき
- release candidate を更新するとき
- maintainer が repository map の更新を必要と判断したとき

生成物が stale かどうかを毎 PR で強制検査する CI は，初版の範囲外とする．

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LerayHopf.lean` と `LerayHopf/**/*.lean` の file-by-file code LOC を取得できる
- [ ] 空行とコメント行を面積から除外している
- [ ] directory hierarchy を反映した D3 treemap を生成する
- [ ] rectangle の面積が code LOC に比例する
- [ ] top-level module ごとに一貫した色分けを行う
- [ ] 十分な面積の rectangle に file name と LOC を表示する
- [ ] 各 leaf に full path と行数内訳を示す `<title>` がある
- [ ] 出力が JavaScript を含まない standalone SVG である
- [ ] 同じ input から deterministic に同じ配置・色・ラベルを生成できる
- [ ] README または `docs/architecture.md` から図を閲覧できる
- [ ] 図の caption に，面積が code LOC を表すことを明記する
- [ ] 図が証明難度・数学的重要性・品質を表すものではないことが分かる
- [ ] generator dependency が Lean build / Lake package から分離されている
- [ ] Lean source，theorem statement，CI，release attestation を変更しない

## Non-goals

- code coverage の可視化
- theorem / lemma 数による重み付け
- proof difficulty や mathematical importance の推定
- file ごとの GitHub hyperlink
- interactive zoom / search / filtering
- runtime JavaScript を含む HTML dashboard
- 毎 commit の自動更新
- Star History その他の repository metrics との統合
title: [P2][visualization] Lean source の code LOC treemap を生成し repository map として掲載する

## Summary

Restructures `README.md` per issue #188's recommended 8-section layout (title/badges → overview → explore the formalization → main results → scope and limitations → verification status → getting started → documentation/contributing/citation/license), aimed at a general mathematician / Lean-user / PDE-researcher audience reading the public repository for the first time.

- Features the interactive notes site (https://uda-lab.github.io/leray-hopf-notes/) prominently from the top, with a description of what it shows (Lean declarations, dependency graph, Japanese exposition, proof status).
- Removes issue/PR-number references and development-history narration; describes the current result and structure only.
- Keeps claims at the exact Lean-statement level: 𝕋³ and ℝ³ Leray–Hopf weak-solution existence, both capstones kernel-only (no project axioms, no `sorryAx`); explicitly states regularity/uniqueness/non-uniqueness are not claimed; distinguishes `import LerayHopf` (release surface) from `import LerayHopf.Experimental` (isolated opt-in).
- README is 112 lines, down from 203 (~55%), without treating line-count reduction as the goal — the short scope-limitation bullets are kept, just moved to their concise form.
- No Lean source, theorem statement, or Lean API was touched. Docs-only change; no `lake build` needed.

## Content moved

| Content | Moved to |
|---|---|
| Detailed field-by-field claims table | `docs/claims-and-scope.md` (new) |
| Detailed modeling-scope bullets (README keeps the short version) | `docs/claims-and-scope.md` (new) |
| Import guide table (per-import sorry/axiom status) | `docs/claims-and-scope.md` (new) |
| Repository hygiene: dead-file count, docstring coverage, exact `sorry` file:line inventory, statement-card pointer | `docs/STATUS.md` (new "Repository hygiene" section — STATUS.md is already the axiom/sorry ledger) |
| Historical archive/roadmap document list (`docs/archive/milestone.md`, `leray_hopf_lean_mvp_plan.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `REPORT.md`) | `docs/architecture.md` (new "History and provenance" section) |
| Long attestation operational note under the badge | Shrunk to one sentence in README; full detail already lived in `docs/build-and-checks.md` (unchanged, just now the sole home) |

No provenance document was deleted; `docs/archive/*` content stays in place, just linked from `docs/architecture.md` instead of `README.md`.

## Links verified (all HTTP 200 / resolve at this branch)

- https://uda-lab.github.io/leray-hopf-notes/ — 200
- https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/actions/workflows/release-attestation.yml — 200
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/claims-and-scope.md`, `docs/build-and-checks.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CITATION.cff`, `LICENSE`, `LerayHopf/` — all exist at branch HEAD
- Internal links added to `docs/claims-and-scope.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/architecture.md` (to each other, to `../README.md`, to `postmortems/...`, to `archive/...`) — all resolve

## Test plan

- [x] Every relative link in the four touched files resolves against the working tree.
- [x] Both external URLs return HTTP 200.
- [x] `grep -n "issue #\|PR #"` on README.md returns nothing.

Related: #188

## 背景

`leray-hopf` は，3次元トーラスおよび全空間 `ℝ³` における Leray–Hopf 弱解存在を Lean 4 + mathlib で形式化した public repository である．公開後の認知や関心の推移を把握する補助的な指標として，GitHub star 数の時間変化を継続的に確認できるようにする．

star 数は数学的品質や研究上の価値を直接表す指標ではない．本件では，公開後の visibility / dissemination の推移を記録する補助的なメトリクスとしてのみ扱う．

README の一般読者向け再構成は #188 で扱い，本件は Star History 導入だけを別 PR で実施する．README の大規模編集と競合させないため，原則として #188 の構成確定後に着手する．

## 方針

外部サービス [Star History](https://www.star-history.com/) の標準的な手描き風グラフを利用する．自前の定期 workflow，CSV 保存，SVG 生成基盤はこの段階では導入しない．

2026年7月以降の GitHub API 制限に対応するため，repository owner が `uda-lab/leray-hopf` のみに限定した fine-grained personal access token を作成し，Star History の公式な認証付き embed 手順を用いる．

必要な権限は最小限とし，対象 repository の metadata / stargazer 情報を読み取るための read-only 権限だけを与える．token の平文を README，issue，repository secret，workflow log その他の repository 資産へ保存しない．

参考：

- Star History: https://www.star-history.com/
- Star History setup guide: https://www.star-history.com/blog/how-to-use-github-star-history/
- GitHub REST API — Starring: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/activity/starring

## Scope

- Star History 上で `uda-lab/leray-hopf` の履歴グラフを生成する
- Star History の標準的な手描き風表示を採用する
- README にグラフまたはグラフへの明確な導線を追加する
- README 上での表示位置・大きさ・見出しを #188 の一般読者向け構成と整合させる
- 認証 token は repository 単位・read-only・必要最小限とする
- token の期限，失効，rotation 時の再設定手順を maintainer 向けに短く記録する
- 認証していない一般閲覧者から README 上のグラフが正常に表示されることを確認する

## README 上の扱い

star history は研究成果の主説明ではないため，README 冒頭の overview や main results より前には置かない．

候補位置：

- `Project visibility` / `Community interest` 等の短い節
- Documentation / citation より前後の補助的な位置
- 折りたたみ表示または小さな chart + 詳細ページへのリンク

最終位置は #188 の README 構成に従う．成果の意義，main theorem，interactive notes への導線を圧迫しないこと．

## セキュリティ・運用

- fine-grained token の対象を `uda-lab/leray-hopf` のみに限定する
- write / administration 権限を与えない
- token の平文を commit，README，issue，PR，Actions secret，log に保存しない
- Star History が生成する埋め込み値以外を repository に置かない
- token の有効期限を設定し，期限切れ時の更新方法を owner 向けに記録する
- Star History の仕様変更・サービス停止時には，壊れた画像を README に放置せず，埋め込みを除去または代替する

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Star History の公式手順で `uda-lab/leray-hopf` の履歴グラフを生成した
- [ ] token は対象 repository のみ，read-only，必要最小限の権限に制限されている
- [ ] token の平文が repository 内および公開 issue / PR に含まれていない
- [ ] README から star 数の推移を確認できる
- [ ] 未認証の一般閲覧者からグラフが正常に表示される
- [ ] 手描き風の標準表示を採用している
- [ ] README の main results，日本語インタラクティブノート，verification status より視覚的に優先されていない
- [ ] #188 の README 構成と競合しない独立 PR として実装する
- [ ] token の失効・期限切れ時の再設定手順が maintainer 向けに記録されている
- [ ] star 数を数学的品質や形式化の正当性の指標として説明していない

## Non-goals

- star 数を研究品質・引用数・数学的正当性の代替指標として扱うこと
- stargazer 個人の収集・分析
- 他 repository とのランキング比較
- clone / traffic / view / follower 等の追加メトリクス収集
- 自前の star-history workflow，CSV，SVG 生成基盤の構築
- Star History 導入のための theorem statement，Lean source，CI，release attestation の変更
title: [P2][metrics] Star History を導入し GitHub star 数の推移を可視化する

body:
## 背景

現在の `README.md` は，Leray–Hopf 弱解存在の形式化成果を正確に説明している一方で，一般読者向けの研究概要，capstone theorem の厳密な主張範囲，release attestation の運用説明，import cone の技術仕様，残存 `sorry` の個別情報，statement review の事後検証，agent / maintainer 向け文書案内までを一つの入口に集約している．

公開後の repository の README としては情報量が過剰であり，成果の意義と読み始める場所が見えにくい．README は一般読者向けの概要に集中させ，厳密な技術情報は既存または新設の専門文書へ移す．

## 目的

README を，形式化研究に関心をもつ数学者，Lean 利用者，PDE・数値解析研究者が最初に読む公開文書として再構成する．

特に，次の公開ノートを README と並ぶ主要な入口として，冒頭から明確に案内する．

- **Interactive notes / 日本語解説:** https://uda-lab.github.io/leray-hopf-notes/

このサイトでは Lean 宣言，依存関係，日本語の数学的説明，証明状態を閲覧できることを簡潔に説明する．

## 推奨構成

### 1. Title / badges

release-attestation badge は維持する．ただし badge 直下の長い運用上の注意書きは一文程度に縮め，詳細は `docs/build-and-checks.md` へ委ねる．

### 2. Overview

冒頭の数段落だけで，次を理解できるようにする．

- Lean 4 + mathlib による形式化である
- 3次元非圧縮 Navier–Stokes 方程式を対象とする
- 3次元トーラスと全空間 `ℝ³` の双方について Leray–Hopf 型弱解の存在を形式化した
- 二つの capstone theorem は project axiom と `sorryAx` に依存しない
- regularity，uniqueness，non-uniqueness は主張していない

成果の規模や数学的意義は明確に述べるが，Lean 宣言の型を越えた主張はしない．

### 3. Explore the formalization

README 上部に，次の導線をまとめる．

- 日本語インタラクティブノート
- Lean source
- architecture overview
- exact claims / scope
- citation information

### 4. Main results

二つの capstone theorem を簡潔に紹介する．完全な Lean signature を掲載する場合も，その直後の説明は一般読者向けの短い文章に留める．

現在の詳細な claims table は README から分離し，例えば `docs/claims-and-scope.md` へ移す．既存文書へ統合する場合は，README から一意に到達できるようにする．

### 5. Scope and limitations

README には次の重要事項だけを短く残す．

- 外力なし
- 任意の有限時間区間 `[0,T]`
- トーラスの周期規約
- weak formulation の test class
- regularity / uniqueness / non-uniqueness は対象外
- Experimental 層は通常の `import LerayHopf` から分離されている

個別 field の一覧や「何を主張しないか」の長大な表は専門文書へ移す．

### 6. Verification status

次を簡潔に説明する．

- `import LerayHopf` は `sorry`・project axiom を含まない release surface
- exact release candidate は手動 attestation で検証する
- incomplete な追加研究は `LerayHopf.Experimental` に隔離されている

workflow 条件，guard script の全列挙，残存 `sorry` の行番号一覧は README に置かない．

### 7. Getting started

一般利用者が必要とする最小限を掲載する．

```lean
import LerayHopf
```

基本的な build command を示し，詳細な import matrix と CI policy は専門文書へ移す．

### 8. Documentation / contributing / citation / license

主要文書への導線を簡潔にまとめる．内部 agent 文書，scratch 文書，過去の milestone 文書は README の主要ナビゲーションから外す．必要なら maintainer-facing documentation から辿れるようにする．

## README から削除・移動する内容

- heading や本文に含まれる issue / PR 番号
- issue / PR に沿った実装経緯の説明
- 過去の statement defect と postmortem の詳細
- 残存 `sorry` の正確なファイル名・行番号一覧
- guard script の実装仕様の逐次説明
- agent workflow，review protocol，scratch directory の案内
- historical roadmap / campaign の一覧
- `pdelib` 移管計画など，本 repository の利用開始に不要な将来計画

これらは必要に応じて `docs/STATUS.md`，`docs/build-and-checks.md`，`docs/architecture.md`，`docs/statement-gates.md`，`docs/postmortems/`，maintainer-facing documentation へ移す．provenance 文書自体は削除しない．

## 編集方針

- README から issue / PR 番号への参照を原則として除去する
- 過去の開発経緯ではなく，現在の成果と構造に基づいて説明する
- 一般読者向けの説明と，形式的保証の厳密な記録を分離する
- 数学的な但し書きを削り過ぎず，重要な scope limitation は短く維持する
- 宣伝的な誇張は避けるが，`𝕋³`・`ℝ³` 双方の存在定理を kernel-only で形式化した成果は明確に打ち出す
- README の長さは現行のおよそ半分を一つの目安とするが，行数削減自体を目的にしない

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] README 冒頭から日本語インタラクティブノートへ明確に到達できる
- [ ] 最初の画面内で，対象方程式，二つの領域，主要成果，検証状態が理解できる
- [ ] issue / PR 番号に依存した説明が残っていない
- [ ] 過去の開発経緯ではなく，現在の成果と構造に基づいて記述されている
- [ ] 詳細な claims table，attestation policy，Experimental inventory が適切な専門文書へ移されている
- [ ] `import LerayHopf` と `LerayHopf.Experimental` の区別が簡潔かつ正確に説明されている
- [ ] 数学的 scope limitation が capstone の exact claim と一致する
- [ ] README 内の公開 URL と文書リンクを実地確認する
- [ ] Lean source，theorem statement，proof status は変更しない

## Non-goals

- theorem statement や Lean API の変更
- architecture documentation 全体の書き直し
- postmortem・provenance 文書の削除
- star 数履歴の実装。本件とは別 issue で扱う
title: [P1][docs] README を一般読者向けの入口として再構成する

Parent / follow-up: #150

Related:

- #185
- PR #186
- notes-side Pages gate: `uda-lab/leray-hopf-notes#32`

## 背景

release-candidate SHA `7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5` に対する `release-attestation` が成功した．この workflow は，exact SHA，`lean-toolchain`，`lake-manifest.json` の SHA-256，full `lake build`，各 discipline guard，capstone live axiom pin の結果を記録する．

しかし，現在の保存先には期限がある．

- workflow artifact `release-attestation-<sha>` は 90 日で失効する．
- job summary と workflow run log も Actions の保持期間に依存する．
- 現在の artifact には `attestation.md` と guard logs は含まれるが，full `lake build` の生ログは workflow run log 側にしかない．

実際の公開 release に対応する証跡として残すなら，GitHub Release asset に複製し，workflow run の保持期限から独立させる必要がある．

## 方針

今回の attested SHA に対応する tag / GitHub Release を作成し，証跡一式を asset として添付する．まだ正式版番号を付けない場合は，例として `v0.1.0-rc1` または日付付き RC tag を用い，GitHub Release を pre-release として作成する．tag は必ず attested SHA `7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5` を直接指すものとする．

Release asset には最低限，次を含める．

1. `attestation.md`
2. workflow artifact 全体を保持した `release-attestation-<sha>.zip`
3. successful run の full job log，例 `release-attestation-run-<run-id>.log.gz`
4. 上記全 asset の `SHA256SUMS`
5. 小さな機械可読記録 `release-provenance.json`

`release-provenance.json` には少なくとも次を記録する．

- repository
- release tag
- attested commit SHA
- workflow run URL / run id
- workflow file path
- workflow definition を実行した branch / commit
- `lean-toolchain`
- `lake-manifest.json` SHA-256
- 実行開始・終了時刻
- 各 asset のファイル名と SHA-256

## 一回限りの手順

- [ ] 最新の successful `release-attestation` run を開き，job summary の attested SHA が `7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5` であることを確認する．
- [ ] workflow artifact `release-attestation-<sha>` をダウンロードする．
- [ ] `gh run view <run-id> --repo uda-lab/leray-hopf --log > release-attestation-run-<run-id>.log` 等で full run log を保存し，gzip 圧縮する．
- [ ] artifact を展開し，`attestation.md`，guard logs，run log の内容を確認する．秘密情報やローカル絶対パスが含まれていないことも軽く走査する．
- [ ] exact SHA を指す annotated tag を作成する．例：`git tag -a <tag> 7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5 -m "Verified release candidate"`．
- [ ] GitHub Release を作成する．正式公開前なら pre-release とする．
- [ ] `attestation.md`，artifact zip，full run log，`release-provenance.json`，`SHA256SUMS` を Release asset として添付する．
- [ ] Release note に「この証跡は current HEAD ではなく exact SHA のみを認証する」と明記する．
- [ ] README または `docs/build-and-checks.md` から該当 Release / asset へ到達できるリンクを追加する．workflow 一覧への badge は残してよいが，恒久証跡への導線を別途置く．

## 将来の attestation に対する運用

workflow の成功だけで自動的に Release を作成しない．release candidate の採用は owner 判断なので，次のいずれかとする．

- 当面は owner が成功 run を確認した後，手動スクリプトで Release asset 化する．
- 将来は `workflow_dispatch` の明示 input（例 `publish_release_assets=true` と tag）を追加し，owner が指定した場合だけ draft / pre-release を作成する．

自動化する場合も，tag が attested SHA を指すこと，既存 Release を誤って上書きしないこと，asset checksum を生成することを fail-closed に検証する．

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] attested SHA を直接指す tag と GitHub Release が存在する．
- [ ] `attestation.md`，guard logs を含む artifact zip，full workflow log，`release-provenance.json`，`SHA256SUMS` が Release asset として取得できる．
- [ ] asset の checksum が相互検証できる．
- [ ] Release note が exact-SHA semantics と workflow run URL を明示する．
- [ ] Actions artifact / run が失効した後も，公開 repository から証跡一式へ到達できる．
- [ ] notes-side #32 から，source release attestation の恒久 URL を参照できる．
title: [P1][release] release-attestation 証跡を GitHub Release asset として恒久保存する

body:
## Root cause

Closes the gap analyzed in #185:

1. `scripts/print_axioms.lean` (line 40, added for #158's Experimental axiom-profile visibility) has `import LerayHopf.Experimental`.
2. `release-attestation.yml`'s build step (`leanprover/lean-action`, plain `lake build`) builds only `defaultTargets = ["LerayHopf"]` — `LerayHopf.Experimental` is deliberately not a default target, so its olean was never produced in the runner.
3. `lake env lean scripts/print_axioms.lean` does not build missing imports; it failed immediately on the missing module.
4. In `check-axioms-live.sh`, the failing command substitution `OUTPUT="$(...)"` under `set -euo pipefail` aborted the script before `echo "$OUTPUT"`, so the underlying lean error was swallowed — hence the near-empty log in the failed run ([29712522859](https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/actions/runs/29712522859)).

## Fix (attestation harness only — no Lean source touched, candidate SHA does not move)

1. `.github/workflows/release-attestation.yml`: add a `Build Experimental opt-in module (required by check-axioms-live)` step (id `build_experimental`, `continue-on-error: true`, logged to `logs/build-experimental.log`) immediately after the main build step. Wired into all three aggregation points: the `OUTCOME` associative array in "Compose attestation record", the markdown summary table (row placed right after the full `lake build` row), and the outcome list in "Fail job if any step failed".
2. `scripts/check-axioms-live.sh`: hardened the `lake env lean` invocation to capture its exit status outside of `errexit` (`set +e` / `set -e` around the capture), always echo `$OUTPUT`, and on nonzero exit print a targeted diagnostic pointing at `lake build LerayHopf.Experimental` before exiting 1. Both the `flock` and non-`flock` branches are preserved (command built once into an array, `set -euo pipefail` semantics unchanged for the rest of the script).

## Verification

- YAML sanity: `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/release-attestation.yml'))"` → OK.
- Shell sanity: `bash -n scripts/check-axioms-live.sh` → OK. `shellcheck scripts/check-axioms-live.sh` → only 2 pre-existing SC2086 info-level findings at lines 160/164 (in `assert_axioms`, unrelated to and untouched by this diff); no new findings.
- Functional test, done safely against the warm `.lake` in the main clone `/workspaces/lean-pde` (currently checked out at `7c15710`, the exact candidate SHA) **without modifying anything under that clone**: created a `cp -al` (hardlinked) scratch copy of the full clone at `/workspaces/scratch/attest-test-185`, then broke the hardlink (`cp --remove-destination`) only for the specific files under test before editing them, verifying via `stat -c '%i'` and `git status`/`git diff` on the original clone that it stayed byte-identical throughout. Scratch dir removed after testing.
  - **Positive test**: ran the patched `check-axioms-live.sh` (hardlink-broken copy) against the scratch tree, whose `.lake` already had `LerayHopf.Experimental.olean` built (hardlinked from the warm clone). Result: exit 0, all 4 pins OK, Experimental-module axiom profile printed as expected (`AXIOM LIVE PIN OK`).
  - **Negative test** (proves the hardening works): in the same scratch tree, broke the hardlink for `scripts/print_axioms.lean` and appended a bogus `import LerayHopf.DoesNotExist`. Re-ran the patched script: it now prints the underlying lean error (`object file '.../DoesNotExist.olean' ... does not exist`) plus the new diagnostic (`ERROR: 'lake env lean scripts/print_axioms.lean' failed with exit 1` + the `lake build LerayHopf.Experimental` pointer) and exits 1 — previously this failure mode produced no error text at all.
- **Not tested**: the workflow YAML itself cannot be exercised locally (no `act` available); the added step and its wiring into the three aggregation points were verified by YAML lint + manual reading, not by an actual Actions run.

## After merge

Re-dispatch `release-attestation` from branch `main` with `ref` input `7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5` — the attested SHA is unchanged; the frozen-candidate ruling stands.

Refs #185
title: release-attestation: build Experimental opt-in module before check-axioms-live (#185)

body:
## Failure

release-attestation run https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/actions/runs/29712522859 (ref = release candidate S = 7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5) failed at the `check-axioms-live.sh` guardrail (step 12), exit 1 approximately 1.5 s after start, with no error text beyond `==> Running live #print axioms pin...`.

## Root cause

1. `scripts/print_axioms.lean` (line 40, added for #158 Experimental axiom-profile visibility) has `import LerayHopf.Experimental`.
2. The workflow's build step (leanprover/lean-action, plain `lake build`) builds only `defaultTargets = ["LerayHopf"]` — `LerayHopf.Experimental` is deliberately NOT a default target, so its olean is never produced in the runner.
3. `lake env lean scripts/print_axioms.lean` does not build missing imports; it fails immediately on the missing module.
4. In `check-axioms-live.sh`, the failing command substitution `OUTPUT="$(...)"` under `set -euo pipefail` aborts the script before `echo "$OUTPUT"`, so the underlying lean error is swallowed — hence the near-empty log.

The same gap has bitten twice locally (silent check-axioms-live deaths on missing Experimental.olean). It is invisible to routine CI because check-axioms-live runs only in this manual attestation workflow.

## Fix (attestation harness only — candidate SHA S does not move)

1. `.github/workflows/release-attestation.yml`: add an explicit `lake build LerayHopf.Experimental` step (own id, `continue-on-error: true`, logged to `logs/`) between the main build and the guardrails, and include its outcome in the attestation record table and the final fail-if-any-failed aggregation.
2. `scripts/check-axioms-live.sh`: harden the `lake env lean` invocation so a nonzero exit prints the captured output and a clear diagnostic (pointing at `lake build LerayHopf.Experimental`) instead of dying silently. (This part benefits future candidates; the S checkout uses S's copy of the script, which is fine because the workflow-level build step alone makes the S run pass.)

## Effect on the frozen ruling

None on the candidate: `workflow_dispatch` executes the workflow definition from the branch selected in the Actions UI (main), while `inputs.ref` determines the attested checkout. After this fix merges to main, re-dispatching with `ref = 7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5` attests exactly S; the frozen-candidate ruling (notes#32) remains valid.
title: [P0][release-blocker] release-attestation: check-axioms-live fails — LerayHopf.Experimental olean not built by the workflow's default-target build

Parent: #145

**Priority: P2 — post-release acceptable maintenance.**

## 背景

owner が current main で `lake build` を実行したところ，build 自体は成功したが，project source から多数の linter / deprecation warning が再生・出力された。

監査 snapshot:

- source HEAD: `7c15710a7b9068a2aa105fc7c11b432e7685b7b5`
- result: `Build completed successfully (3189 jobs).`
- warnings: **137 warnings / 37 files**
- `sorry`、未解決 metavariable、kernel/soundness、build failure に関する警告はなし

したがって数学的正当性や公開可否を直ちに左右する問題ではない。一方で、警告が多いと新しい重要な警告が埋もれ、deprecated API は将来の mathlib 更新で破損要因になるため、一度まとめて解消する。

この issue では警告を種別ごとに別 issue へ分割せず、一つの maintenance cleanup として扱う。

## Triage

| 種別 | 件数 | 方針 |
|---|---:|---|
| named variable が明示的に参照されない | 61 | 意味と公開 API を確認し、削除または `_name` 化 |
| unused simp argument | 42 | 不要な simp 引数を除去 |
| deprecated API / tactic | 20 | 警告が示す現行 API へ移行 |
| no-op tactic | 6 | 効果のない tactic を除去・簡素化 |
| unnecessary `simpa` | 3 | `simp` へ簡素化 |
| unused section variable | 2 | `omit` または section 変数の scope を縮小 |
| unreachable tactic | 2 | tactic chain を書き直す |
| tactic sequencing style | 1 | 等価な簡潔形へ修正 |

### Deprecated API の内訳

- 5 × `mul_le_mul_left'` → `mul_le_mul_right`
- 4 × `MeasureTheory.integral_finset_sum` → `MeasureTheory.integral_finsetSum`
- 2 × `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_eq_lintegral_rpow_enorm` → `…_toReal`
- 2 × `continuous_finset_sum` → `continuous_finsetSum`
- 1 × `MeasureTheory.integrable_finset_sum` → `MeasureTheory.integrable_finsetSum`
- 1 × `Set.mem_diff` → `Set.mem_sdiff`
- 1 × `Set.left_mem_Ici` → `Set.self_mem_Ici`
- 1 × `zero_le'` → `zero_le`
- 1 × `AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum` → `AEMeasurable.tsum`
- 1 × `Real.tendsto_of_bddAbove_monotone` → `tendsto_atTop_ciSup`
- 1 × deprecated `push_neg` usage → `push Not`

## Important distinction for `unusedVariables`

この警告を「仮定が数学的に不要」と機械的に解釈しない。

- **意図的に維持する interface condition:** binder 自体は残し、名前だけ `_hrep` 等にする。例: `FrechetKolmogorovInput.precompact_of_uniform_modulus` の representation 条件。
- **frozen / compatibility signature:** 型を維持する必要がある場合は `_hu` 等にし、既存コメントと整合させる。例: `galerkinP_preserves_sigma` の `hu`。
- **真に不要な theorem hypothesis:** theorem を実際に強めることが妥当で、call sites への影響を確認できる場合だけ削除する。
- **自動包含された不要な typeclass:** `omit` を使う。候補は `timeConvL2_norm_le` の `[CompleteSpace E]`、`energy_hasDerivAt_of_solution` の `[FiniteDimensional ℝ V]`。
- **局所 proof binder:** 削除または `_name` 化する。

確認すべき代表例:

- `solution_agree` の `hab`
- `H1_ball_uniform_L2_approx` の `hM0`
- `exists_goodSample` の `hnn`
- `restrictToBall_comp_curve_memLp` の `hν`, `hT`
- `galerkin_reg_bound` の `hν`
- `galerkin_weakLimit_R3` の `hφ`, `hT`
- weak-limit / compactness 系定理に残る `B`, `hH1`, `hvf`, `hψ`

## Required work

- [ ] 137 warnings を current source で再現し、種別と occurrence を記録する
- [ ] deprecated API / tactic 20件を現行 API へ移行する
- [ ] unused simp arguments 42件を除去する
- [ ] no-op / unreachable / unnecessary tactic を簡素化する
- [ ] unused section variables を `omit` または scope 整理で解消する
- [ ] unused named variables 61件を上記基準で個別に判定する
- [ ] 公開 theorem / structure field の binder を削除する場合、型の変更と downstream call sites を明示する
- [ ] 意図的に残す仮定は、型を変えずに underscore name と必要最小限の理由コメントで処理する
- [ ] 警告を隠す repository-wide `set_option linter.… false` は追加しない
- [ ] 変更対象 module と downstream を build する
- [ ] 最終的に `lake build` で project source 由来の警告が残らないことを確認する

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] build が成功する
- [ ] project source 由来の上記137 warnings が0件になる
- [ ] deprecated declaration が残らない
- [ ] repository-wide linter suppression を導入していない
- [ ] theorem conclusion、proof status、axiom inventory を変更していない
- [ ] 公開 API の仮定を削除した箇所は、数学的に妥当な strengthening であり、全 call sites が build する
- [ ] warning cleanup 以外の proof refactor や module 分割を混在させない

## Non-blocking classification

現状は full build green であり、soundness / `sorry` / declaration failure の警告はないため release blocker ではない。P2 として扱い、P0/P1 の公開作業を妨げない。

body:
Refs #178

## What

`LerayHopf/Experimental.lean`'s module-header doc comment (the bullet describing
`LerayHopf.Bochner.TimeSobolevExperimental`) used the ill-formed notation

```
W^{1,2}(0,T;V) ∩ L^2(0,T;V') ↪ C([0,T];H)
```

The intersection form is mathematically malformed as written — the two spaces have
incompatible membership conditions stated this way. This PR replaces it with the
correct set-builder form:

```
{u ∈ L²(0,T;V) : u' ∈ L²(0,T;V')} ↪ C([0,T];H)
```

matching the fix already applied to the theorem docstring and TODO comment inside
`LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolevExperimental.lean` itself by PR #179 (merge `105c6594`).

## Why this occurrence was missed before

This occurrence dates from commit `2f0fa1d` (issue #158 era) and lives in
`LerayHopf/Experimental.lean`, not `TimeSobolevExperimental.lean` — it was outside
PR #177's diff, so neither PR #177 nor PR #179's audits touched it. It was found by a
repo-wide grep for the malformed pattern during issue #178's final integration pass;
see [issue #178 comment 5015813089](https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/issues/178#issuecomment-5015813089).

## Scope

Prose-only, one line changed. No rewording of surrounding text beyond the notation
substitution itself; no Lean declarations, no statement cards, no notes-repo content
affected (this file is doc-comment-only, outside the release cone).

## Verification

```
$ git grep -n "W\^{1,2}" -- LerayHopf/
```
returns zero matches after this change (confirmed before commit). The only other
repo-wide occurrence of a similar-looking string, `HANDOFF.md:122`, is a different,
well-formed notation (`W^{1,2}(0,T;X)` alone, no malformed intersection) and is
correctly out of scope for this fix.

**Build gate — exactly what ran, where, and what it covers.** Two separate builds ran
for this PR; they cover different targets and neither is a substitute for the other:

1. **Pre-push hook gate build** (triggered automatically by `git push`, via
   `scripts/hooks/pre-push`): `flock /tmp/lean-build.lock lake build` with no
   explicit target, i.e. `lakefile.toml`'s `defaultTargets = ["LerayHopf"]`. **This
   target does *not* include `LerayHopf.Experimental`** (`Experimental.lean` is
   intentionally outside the release cone and outside `defaultTargets` — see the
   file's own header comment). Output:
   ```
   [pre-push] grep guards…
   OK: no unmarked 'sorry' in Lean sources.
   OK: no undeclared axiom/constant/opaque/unsafe in Lean sources.
   OK: no overclaiming declaration names in Lean sources.
   [pre-push] Lean sources changed — incremental build (serialized)…
   [pre-push] build green
   [pre-push] gate passed
   ```
   The hook does not echo a job count on success (it only tails the log on
   failure); the evidence is exit 0 and the status lines above.

2. **Targeted build of the actually-changed file**, run manually after a sibling
   agent flagged that (1) doesn't cover `Experimental.lean`:
   ```
   $ flock /tmp/lean-build.lock lake build LerayHopf.Experimental
   ...
   ✔ [2767/2767] Built LerayHopf.Experimental (27s)
   Build completed successfully (2767 jobs).
   ```
   Run against the warm/shared `.lake` cache (hardlink-copied from the main clone).
   2767 jobs is the transitive dependency closure of `LerayHopf.Experimental`
   (effectively the whole library plus `Experimental.lean` itself, since nothing
   else imports it); this is the build that actually re-elaborates the file
   containing this PR's one-line change and confirms it compiles.

No other build ran. Static guards (`check-no-sorry.sh`, `check-no-axiom.sh`,
`check-theorem-names.sh`) ran as part of the pre-push hook only (step 1 above); they
are text-grep guards, not target-scoped, so they do cover this file.

## Review

- Codex pre-review (`/codex:review`, foreground, against the branch diff): "The
  change only corrects explanatory documentation for the experimental Lions–Magenes
  statement and does not affect Lean code or theorem interfaces." No findings.
- Broker review (`REVIEW_ACQUIRE_SCRIPT`, codex route) requested and received as a
  top-level comment (not a formal Review API entry):
  https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/pull/183#issuecomment-5015835200 — "Codex
  Review: Didn't find any major issues. Chef's kiss." (reviewed commit `1bca24ca5d`,
  matching this PR's HEAD). Recorded via a `Reviewed-by: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`
  artifact comment on this PR.

Refs #152

## Summary

Picks up the two acceptance-criteria bullets left open by PR #173's mechanical inventory: measure actual heartbeat consumption for the 31 previously-un-annotated declaration-local `maxHeartbeats` overrides and lower any where measurement shows a large safety margin.

## Methodology limitation (read before the table)

Measurement used Mathlib's `#count_heartbeats in` (`Mathlib.Util.CountHeartbeats`), which wraps a single declaration in `set_option maxHeartbeats 0 in` and reports the heartbeats actually consumed. **This isolated per-declaration measurement is not a reliable predictor of whether the real sequential build survives under the measured (or default) budget.** Four declarations measured at 1300–4300 heartbeats — nowhere near the 200000 default — nonetheless timed out at `whnf` when their override was fully removed and rebuilt in the file's real context:

- `R3/AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean`: `weakFormNS_galerkinTest_limit` (measured ~1348)
- `R3/FrechetKolmogorov.lean`: `totallyBounded_image_of_equicont_bdd` (measured ~1629)
- `R3/CurlDensity.lean`: `orthogonalCurl_longitudinal_ae` (measured ~4339)
- `Torus/EnergyConvection.lean`: `convSummand_norm_summable` (measured ~540)

No confirmed root cause — plausibly elaboration deferred outside the measured command span — but the practical consequence is procedural: **an override was only finalized as "removed" or "lowered" in this PR when the exact final file content (no `#count_heartbeats`, no override, or the lowered value) was independently rebuilt end-to-end and confirmed green.** Everywhere that direct rebuild was not performed (either because an earlier direct rebuild in the same file already demonstrated the unreliability, or because of a mid-session shared-build-cache incident that froze all builds for the remainder of the session — see below), the override was **restored to its original, pre-PR value** with a comment recording the measured figure and this reason. Restoring to the original value carries no build risk, since that value already builds successfully in `main`.

A shared-build-cache incident (unrelated `.lake`/mathlib package delete+reclone triggered by a concurrent agent's pre-push hook) froze all `lake build` activity for part of this session; `R3/GoodRepresentative.lean`'s two declarations were measured afterward (`perTest_lipschitz_R3` ~2360, `exists_weak_representative_R3` ~3526) and restored to their original value with the same conservative policy as the other 18.

**Separately**, the same recovery build also caught a real syntax bug (unrelated to heartbeats): five `set_option maxHeartbeats ... in` insertions in `R3/ConvectionForm.lean` had landed *after* the docstring's closing `-/` instead of before its opening `/--` — Lean requires `set_option ... in` to precede the whole declaration including its docstring. A systematic scan across all 14 touched files caught two more instances of the same ordering mistake in `Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean`. All seven are fixed and verified (every `set_option` block now immediately precedes a docstring or declaration keyword, checked mechanically across the full changed-file set).

## Outcome table (31 declarations)

Totals: 7 removed (direct-verified), 4 kept at original with direct-verified-unsafe evidence, 20 kept at original conservatively (measured but not independently re-verified at a lower value).

## Validation

Exact commands run against this branch's final commit, each with its scope stated explicitly:

1. Full default-target build: `lake build` (target `LerayHopf`, the `lakefile.toml` `defaultTargets`) — **`Build completed successfully (3189 jobs)`**. This covers all 14 touched files and their full transitive closure, including both capstones.
2. `LerayHopf.Experimental` explicit build (opt-in module, not part of the default target, required by `scripts/print_axioms.lean`): `lake build LerayHopf.Experimental` — **`Build completed successfully (2767 jobs)`**.
3. `scripts/agent-preflight.sh`, run standalone (it takes `flock /tmp/lean-build.lock` internally — do not wrap it in an outer flock, that self-deadlocks) — all 8 gates green: `check-no-sorry.sh`, `check-no-axiom.sh`, `check-theorem-names.sh`, `check-axioms.sh`, `check-release-cone.sh`, `test-check-release-cone.sh`, `check-statement-cards.sh`, `check-axioms-live.sh`.
4. `check-axioms-live.sh`'s live `#print axioms` pin specifically: both capstones (`exists_lerayHopf_torus3`, `exists_lerayHopf_r3`) match `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — kernel-only, 0 project axioms, matching `main`. Both Core representatives (`lower_bound_from_inverse_square_lifespan`, `localCompactness_R3_of_ballCompact`) are Core-clean (no project axioms, no `sorryAx`). `AXIOM LIVE PIN OK`.
5. Repo's own pre-push hook, on push via `git -C /workspaces/lean-pde push origin issue-152-annotate`: grep guards + incremental build ran and passed (`[pre-push] build green`, `[pre-push] gate passed`) before the branch was accepted by the remote.

This build set is the correctness gate for the 20 declarations restored to their original (pre-PR, already-working) value without a dedicated per-declaration re-verification build: since each restored value is byte-for-byte what already builds on `main`, a green full-project build is sufficient evidence for those — no additional rebuild needed.

Direct end-to-end per-file rebuilds (each with the override fully removed or lowered, isolating the change) were additionally performed for: `Analysis/FourierParseval.lean`, `Galerkin/DissipativeODE.lean` (both green with overrides removed); `R3/AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean`, `R3/CurlDensity.lean`, `R3/FrechetKolmogorov.lean`, `Torus/EnergyConvection.lean` (each is where the isolated-`#count_heartbeats`-undercounts pattern was caught — see Methodology limitation above); `R3/EnergyClassConvection.lean`, `Torus/ConvectionForm.lean`, `R3/GoodRepresentative.lean` (green with overrides removed; the last also incidentally re-confirmed the docstring-ordering syntax fixes in `R3/ConvectionForm.lean` and `Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean`, both of which are in its transitive import closure).

body:
Refs #155

## Scope (wave 2 — the remaining heuristic-flagged declarations)

PR #175 (wave 1) triaged `Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean` and `R3/ConvectionExtension.lean`
(39 of the ~90 repo-wide heuristic-flagged declarations). This PR triages the rest: **55
undocumented public declarations across 20 files**, found by regenerating the heuristic scan
on current `main` and excluding the two wave-1 files. No declarations remain undocumented by
this heuristic anywhere in `LerayHopf/` after this PR.

## Triage method

Reused wave 1's heuristic (public `theorem`/`lemma`/`def`/`instance`/`abbrev` with no
immediately preceding `/-- ... -/` docstring), fixing two correctness bugs found while
re-running it:

1. **Prose-inside-comment false positives.** The line-based scan matched prose sentences
   inside multi-line `/-- ... -/` or `/-! ... -/` comments whenever they happened to start
   with a word like "theorem"/"lemma"/"instance" (e.g. "...theorem also satisfies the same
   hypotheses..."). Fixed by tracking block-comment nesting depth across lines instead of
   checking single lines in isolation.
2. **Attribute-separated docstring false positives.** A docstring separated from its
   declaration by a standalone attribute line (`/-- ... -/` then `@[simp]` then `theorem foo`)
   was not recognized as documenting the declaration. Fixed by skipping attribute-only lines
   when searching backward for a docstring.

For each of the resulting 55 candidates: `grep -rlw <name> LerayHopf/` (excluding the defining
file) classified 41 as externally referenced and 14 as local-only. For every local-only
candidate, I read the surrounding file/section context before deciding — this changed the
outcome from a naive "grep says local-only ⇒ privatize" rule in two ways:

- **Two declarations had a real docstring already**, just separated from the declaration by an
  intervening `-- TODO`/domain-guard line-comment block (the same failure mode as bug 2 above,
  but with a `--` block instead of an attribute). Fixed with a pure reorder (docstring moved to
  immediately precede the declaration) — zero content change:
  `Bochner/TimeMollification.lean`'s `timeMollification_exists`,
  `Bochner/TimeSobolev.lean`'s `W1pTime.ofHValuedDeriv` (the domain-of-definition guard comment
  was folded into the docstring body, since it directly explains the theorem's hypotheses).
- **Every other local-only candidate was, on reading, deliberate public API**, not
  implementation-only plumbing: `Analysis/RealComplexLpBridge.lean`'s own header explicitly
  says "All ten declarations were `private` in `EnergyClassConvection.lean`; made public here"
  (`mulRBdd_coeFn` is one of those ten); `R3/SolutionInterfaces.lean` and
  `Torus/SolutionInterfaces.lean`'s five-lemma "domain-projection reduction" blocks are
  introduced by a section header stating they exist so "downstream `rw`/`linarith` sites... keep
  working"; `R3/GalerkinScheme.lean`'s nine-declaration `S1`–`S6`/`D1`–`D6` block (including one
  `instance`) are the literal named fields of the public `R3GalerkinScheme` bundle per their own
  section comments; the remaining few (`ballMassSqrt_nonneg`, `sqrtViscousWeight_nonneg`,
  `continuous_sqrtViscousWeight`, `galerkinSpanToSigma_coe`,
  `FieldForms.inner_self_vectorField`) are standard companion facts about an already-public
  definition, used by other public lemmas in the same file.

**Net result: 0 declarations privatized this wave.** Every candidate that looked
implementation-only from the reference-count heuristic alone turned out, on reading, to be
either mis-flagged (docstring ordering) or intentionally public. This is a different — and
equally honest — outcome from PR #175, which did find and privatize a genuine 24-declaration
internal "analytic engine" block; this wave's files simply didn't contain that pattern.
`instance galerkinSpan_hasOrthogonalProjection` in particular was treated with the extra
caution the plan comment on #155 flagged (typeclass resolution isn't caught by textual grep) —
kept public rather than risk a silent downstream elaboration break for no clear benefit.

No theorem statement's mathematical content changed anywhere in this diff — docstring-only
edits, plus two pure comment-reorders.

## Files changed

`Analysis/{BoundedMultiplier,FourierParseval,RealComplexLpBridge,SpectralWeakGradient,
TensorEdgeGluing}.lean`, `Bochner/{TimeMollification,TimeSobolev}.lean`,
`Galerkin/QuadraticField.lean`, `R3/{ConvectionForm,FrechetKolmogorov,GalerkinODEExistence,
GalerkinScheme,SobolevEmbedding,SolutionInterfaces,WeightedFourierCommute}.lean`,

## Context

PR #177 (merged as 53c9961) fixed the "Literature reference" section notation
and the Temam locator in `docs/statement-cards/w1pTime_continuous_in_H.md`,
but rev-s177's re-review of PR #177 (see
https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/pull/177#issuecomment-5015393715) found
four findings, two of which that merge did not cover. This PR closes those
two remaining findings and documents the status of the other two.

## Per-finding mapping

1. **`LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolevExperimental.lean:46`** (docstring) — the
   malformed `W^{1,2}(0,T;V) ∩ L^2(0,T;V')` replaced with
   `{u ∈ L²(0,T;V) : u' ∈ L²(0,T;V')}`. FIXED in this PR.
2. **Same file, line 67** (TODO comment) — same substitution, "Lions–Magenes
   embedding `{u ∈ L²(0,T;V) : u' ∈ L²(0,T;V')} ↪ C([0,T];H)`." FIXED in this
   PR.
3. **`docs/statement-cards/w1pTime_continuous_in_H.md`, hypothesis-mapping
   table, `hT` row** — the prior justification ("nonempty time interval;
   needed for `ContinuousOn` on `Set.Icc 0 T` to be non-vacuous") is wrong:
   `Set.Icc 0 T` is nonempty for any `T ≥ 0` (`Set.Icc 0 0` is a singleton),
   so `hT : 0 < T` is not needed for that. FIXED in this PR: the row now
   states the real reason — `hT` gives the open interval `Set.Ioo 0 T`
   positive length, which the weak-time-derivative apparatus needs (test
   functions with `tsupport ψ ⊆ Set.Ioo 0 T`, and the du Bois-Reymond bump
   construction `exists_unitMass_weight hT`). Evidence trace (kept out of
   the card per rev-s177's guidance to keep the cell concise):
   - `LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolevAC.lean:97` — `exists_unitMass_weight`
     takes `hT : 0 < T` and builds a `ContDiff`, compactly-supported bump
     `ρ` with `tsupport ρ ⊆ Icc a b ⊂ Ioo 0 T`; the construction needs
     `Ioo 0 T` nonempty (in fact of positive length) to place the bump's
     support strictly inside.
   - `LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolevAC.lean:119,136-141` — the du
     Bois-Reymond-style lemma restricts test functions to
     `K ⊆ Set.Ioo 0 T` and integrates over
     `volume.restrict (Set.Ioo 0 T)`; this is vacuous/degenerate if
     `Set.Ioo 0 T = ∅`, i.e. if `T ≤ 0`.
   - Several `ContDiffBump`/`tsupport` radius computations further down
     the file (e.g. lines 150-233) all rely on there being room strictly
     inside `(0, T)` to place compactly-supported bumps, which requires
     `T > 0` strictly, not just `T ≥ 0`.
4. **Temam locator** ("III.1.2; §III.1.4") — **left unchanged**, per
   rev-s177's explicit instruction not to alter it. **Page-level
   verification of this locator remains OPEN**: two independent reviewers
   (rev-s177 and rev-n97n98) were unable to verify the exact
   lemma/subsection numbering against the cited edition of Temam's
   *Navier–Stokes Equations: Theory and Numerical Analysis* (AMS Chelsea,
   2001 reprint) from available web sources. An owner page-check of the
   physical/PDF edition is required before this checklist item can close.
   This repo's issue #158 postmortem
   (`docs/postmortems/2026-07-w1ptime-false-statement.md`) is precisely
   about shipping unverified named-theorem citations — this PR does not
   repeat that pattern; it explicitly flags the gap instead of closing it
   silently. Also recorded as a comment on issue #178.

## CI / build policy

Per issue #178's CI policy for prose/comment-only changes, **no full
`lake build` was run**. Instead:
- Targeted build of the touched module only:
  `flock /tmp/lean-build.lock lake build LerayHopf.Bochner.TimeSobolevExperimental`
  — succeeded (2750/2750 jobs, only the pre-existing/expected `sorry`
  warning on the declared MONTHS-CLASS residual, no new errors or
  warnings).
- Cheap static guards run and passing:
  `scripts/check-theorem-names.sh`, `scripts/check-statement-cards.sh`,
  `scripts/check-no-axiom.sh`, `scripts/check-no-sorry.sh`.
- The repo's pre-push hook additionally ran its own incremental build gate
  on push and passed ("build green", "gate passed").

Refs #154

## Scope (wave 1 of the split plan)

Split plan posted at https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/issues/154#issuecomment-5011219523.
This PR covers wave 1 exactly: `LerayHopf/R3/SpatialCompactness.lean` only, no other file
touched. `SpatialCompactness.lean` was picked first because it has the lowest import fan-in
of the six candidates (only `R3/Regularity`) and no `maxHeartbeats` overrides to interact with.

`ballLimits_are_consistent` (255 lines) is the largest single declaration across all six
candidate files surveyed for #154. Two dependency-closed blocks of its `have`-chain are
extracted into named top-level `private` lemmas/defs, ahead of the theorem:

1. **Radial classification map** (`ballClassify`, `mem_closedBall_iff_ballClassify_le`,
   `measurable_ballClassify`) — the `c x = ⌈dist x 0⌉₊` device used to partition `Domain3`
   into annuli. Depends only on `Domain3`'s metric structure, not on anything from the
   theorem's binders (`g`, `z`, `ψ`, `M`, …).
2. **Ball-limit consistency** (`ballLimit_furtherRestrict_eq`, `ballLimit_ae_eq_of_le`) —
   the fact that further-restricting the `B_k`-limit to `B_j` (`j ≤ k`) reproduces the
   `B_j`-limit, both as an `Lp`-element equality and as an a.e.-function equality. Depends
   only on `z, ψ, g, hg`.

`ballLimits_are_consistent`'s signature, statement, and the remainder of its proof
(measurability/`MemLp` assembly) are unchanged. No public declaration was renamed, moved,
or had its type changed — only new `private` declarations were added and the two `have`
blocks above now call them instead of duplicating their proofs inline.

Refs #155

## Scope (first tranche)

Issue #155 named `Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean` and the R3 large helper
files as the starting point ("`Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean` と R3 の
大規模 helper files から着手"). This PR covers those two files exactly
(`LerayHopf/Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean`, `LerayHopf/R3/ConvectionExtension.lean`),
39 of the ~90 repo-wide heuristic-flagged declarations. The remaining files
are left for follow-up PRs — tracked as a checklist on #155.

## Triage method

1. Heuristic scan for public (`theorem`/`lemma`/`def`/`instance`/`abbrev`)
   declarations with no preceding `/-- ... -/` docstring. The first pass
   under-counted because it anchored on line-start and missed declarations
   with a same-line `@[simp]` prefix; a corrected scan found 33 candidates
   in the Torus file and 6 in the R3 file (39 total).
2. For each candidate, `grep -rlnw <name> LerayHopf/` across the whole repo
   (excluding the defining file) to classify external vs. local-only usage.
3. Cross-checked `@[simp]`-tagged candidates and their transitive callers so
   that no already-public simp lemma's *statement* would end up naming a
   newly-privatized identifier (this ruled out privatizing `convValW`,
   whose value is directly named in the pre-existing public simp lemma
   `convBLTgalerkin_apply`).
4. One candidate (`velocityProjection_n_eq_of_le`) initially read as
   "documented" because a `/-! ### CLOSURE ... -/` section-header comment
   sat directly above it and confused the doc-detection heuristic; a repo-wide
   grep showed it is used by `ModeCompactness.lean`, `LimitPassage.lean`, and
   `TraceEnergy.lean`, so it was kept public and just given a docstring.

## Disposition

**`LerayHopf/Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean`** — 33 candidates:

- **24 made `private`** — the "ENGINE: analytic core (folded from validated
  ScratchConv)" block: Fourier-coefficient bound/summability lemmas
  (`l2coeff`, `l2coeff_le`, `l2coeff_nonneg`, `tsum_sq_shift`,
  `summable_sq_shift`, `cs_per_m`, `sec_summable`, `dom_summable`,
  `dom_tsum_le`), the complex summand and its algebra
  (`convSummandW`, `convSummandW_norm_summable`, `convSummandW_summable`,
  `coeff_proj_add`, `coeff_proj_smul`), `convValW`'s bound and slot-wise
  linearity (`convValW_bound`, `convValW_add_{u,v,w}`, `convValW_smul_{u,v,w}`),
  and the pre-`convBLTgalerkin` bilinear/BLT construction (`convBilL2Sigma`,
  `convBLTw`, `convBLTw_apply`). All are zero-external-reference (repo-wide
  grep) and none carry `@[simp]` except `convBLTw_apply`, which is
  privatized together with `convBLTw` itself (its LHS pattern can never
  occur outside this file, since `convBLTw` was already the only way to
  construct one).
- **9 kept public, given docstrings**: `subset_galerkinTestSpan` (mirrors
  R3's `subset_schwartzSpan`), `convValW` (forced public per above),
  `convValW_eq_convFormFourier` and `convFormFourier_eq_galerkin` (the T2
  bridge theorems connecting the determined-form value to `convFormFourier`
  and `galerkinConvection`), `isGalerkinTest_add/smul/zero` and
  `mem_galerkinTestSpan_isTest` (closure properties of the `IsGalerkinTest`
  predicate), `convBLTgalerkin_apply` and `convFormL2_def_eq` (existing
  `@[simp]` lemmas that only lacked a docstring).
- **1 additional docstring** on `velocityProjection_n_eq_of_le` (see above;
  not part of the original 33-count, found by re-scanning after fixing the
  section-header detection bug).

**`LerayHopf/R3/ConvectionExtension.lean`** — 6 candidates, all kept public
with new docstrings matching the file's existing "C0/C0b" documentation
style, none privatized: `mem_H1Sigma'_iff`, `H1Sigma'_memH1`,
`subset_schwartzSpan`, `schwartz_mem_H1Sigma'`, `convBLTspanLin_apply`,
`convFormL2_def_eq`.

No theorem statement's mathematical content changed anywhere in this diff
(docstring-only or visibility-only edits).

## Notes-extractor / declaration-corpus impact

`ExtractNotes.lean` extracts **both** public and private declarations (its
record schema carries a `private: Bool` field precisely for this — see the
file's own header comment on `id`/`name` disambiguation for private
helpers). So none of the 24 newly-private Torus declarations disappear from
the corpus on a repin; they change **tier** from public/fully-annotated to
private/lesser-annotation under the notes side's declared two-layer policy.

`leray-hopf-notes` corpus-tier follow-up on next repin):

Closes #156

## Summary

Adds the contributor-facing repository files requested by #156: a `CONTRIBUTING.md`
entry point, a scoped `SECURITY.md`, and issue/PR templates. Also clarifies
`AGENTS.md`'s scope (agent-team-specific, not a policy on human contributors) to
keep the source-of-truth chain consistent with the new contributor-facing docs.
No `.lean` files are touched.

### Added / changed

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — points at `docs/guardrails.md` / `docs/build-and-checks.md` /
  `docs/statement-gates.md` rather than duplicating them, and states:
  - **Build-cost policy**: no single mandatory build gate for contributors. Docs
    /templates-only changes need no build, but do need a link check and (for
    issue templates) YAML front-matter validation — the CI `guards` job checks
    neither (only Lean-discipline textual scans) and may not even trigger on a
    Markdown-only diff (`!**/*.md` in the workflow's path filter), so it is not
    treated as evidence for this bucket. Other non-Lean changes (guard scripts,
    workflows, hooks) need verification proportionate to what changed.
    `.lean`/`lakefile`/`lean-toolchain` changes need a local build, incremental
    at minimum — a full/cold build is optional and welcome, never prohibited.
    `agent-preflight.sh` and the `pre-push` hook are described accurately as
    this project's internal agent-team tooling / a partial local backstop (3 of
    the 7 textual guards plus a conditional build), not mandates on external
    contributors — and that same agent/contributor boundary is now applied
    consistently in `docs/guardrails.md`'s Build-first rule and
    `docs/build-and-checks.md`'s "Mandatory build gate" description, not just in
    `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Full build, live axiom pin, and release-candidate
    attestation stay maintainer-run, on-demand steps.
  - **Statement-changing PR requirement**: any PR adding/changing a public
    theorem/def signature must include a natural-language paraphrase checked
    against the literal Lean type, per `docs/statement-gates.md`'s semantic gate
    and README's Claims-table format (the gate that failed once — see
    `docs/postmortems/2026-07-w1ptime-false-statement.md`).
  - Dependency-update policy: cites the existing maintainer-only `lake update`
    note in `docs/build-and-checks.md`, not invented here.
  - Issue/PR conventions: `[P0]`–`[P3]` title prefix and the priority table in
    #145, `Closes #<n>` / `Refs #<n>`.
- `AGENTS.md` — clarified its own preamble: it is the AI agent team's operating
  procedure (`docs/agent-roles.md`), explicitly not a policy imposed on human
  contributors, who should read `docs/guardrails.md` instead for the substantive
  discipline rules. This removes a source-of-truth contradiction: `AGENTS.md`
  calls itself "canonical, audience-neutral," and SoT order puts it above docs/
  README — so a lower-ranked `CONTRIBUTING.md` could not itself carve external
  contributors out of its hard rules; the carve-out now lives in `AGENTS.md`'s
  own scope statement.
- `SECURITY.md` — scoped to what this repo actually is (no runtime attack
  surface, no user data): routes soundness issues to the theorem-statement
  template, guard bypasses and supply-chain concerns to a plain issue; states
  there is currently no private disclosure channel (no usable public contact
  exists) rather than pointing at one that doesn't work, and no CVE process/SLA.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`, `theorem_statement.md`, `build_failure.md`
  (the three kinds #156 asks for) + `config.yml` (`blank_issues_enabled: true`).
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — `Closes #<n>`, a files/sorry/assumptions
  report section, the statement-changing-PR translation-review checkbox, and a
  validation checklist matching the build-cost policy above (docs/templates-only
  vs. other non-Lean vs. Lean-affecting change, each asking what was actually
  run — no bucket that waives verification for scripts/workflows/hooks).
- `README.md` — one new "Contributing" section pointing at the two new root docs.

### Intentionally not added

- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — this repository has no established conduct-enforcement
  process (reporting contact, escalation path). Adding boilerplate text without
  one would be exactly the "shape without substance" #156's acceptance criteria
  warn against. Recorded as an open decision for the maintainer in
  `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s last section, rather than invented here.
- A separate "dependency update policy" document — the existing
  `docs/build-and-checks.md` note (`lake update` is maintainer-only, pinned via
  `lake-manifest.json`) already covers this; `CONTRIBUTING.md` links to it instead
  of duplicating a new policy.
- Periodic repository description/topics review — listed under #156's "optional
  polish" bullets, not its acceptance criteria; left out of scope for this PR.

## Acceptance criteria (#156)

- [x] contribution policy と build-cost policy を明記 — `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- [x] statement-changing PR に natural-language translation review を要求 —
      `CONTRIBUTING.md` + `.github/pull_request_template.md`
- [x] full build を無条件に contributor へ要求せず，cheap preflight と release
      build を区別 — `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s build-cost policy section (full build
      optional and welcome, not prohibited or mandatory either way)
- [x] security / conduct documents は実際の運用方針に合わせ，形だけの
      boilerplate にしない — `SECURITY.md` is scoped to this repo's actual
      character; `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` deliberately deferred rather than added as
      boilerplate (see above)

## Validation

- No `.lean`, `lakefile`, or `lean-toolchain` files are touched, so there is no
  Lean build target to check. The CI `guards` job (`.github/workflows/lean.yml`)
  did run on this PR and is **green**, but that is not being treated as
  sufficient evidence for the docs/template content itself — `guards` only runs
  the seven Lean-discipline textual scans (`sorry`, axioms, theorem names,
  release cone, statement cards); it does not check markdown links or YAML front
  matter, which is exactly the class of bug (an unquoted-backtick front-matter
  error) that slipped through it during round 1 of this review.
- All markdown links in the new/changed files and all repo-relative paths they
  reference (`docs/...`, `scripts/...`, `.github/workflows/lean.yml`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/statement-cards/`) verified to resolve to existing files, re-checked after
  every revision round.
- All three issue-template YAML front-matter blocks verified to parse with
  `yaml.safe_load` (caught and fixed an unquoted-backtick front-matter bug in
  `build_failure.md` during review).
- Cross-checked every named script, guard, workflow job name (`guards`,
  `full-build`), hook behavior (`scripts/hooks/pre-push`'s actual contents), and
  issue number (#118, #145, #147, #151, #158) against `AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/guardrails.md`, `docs/build-and-checks.md`, `docs/statement-gates.md`,
  `docs/agent-roles.md`, and `.github/workflows/lean.yml`.
- All markdown links and all issue-template YAML front-matter blocks re-verified
  after every revision round (see "Added / changed" above).

## Review history

- A `codex:codex-rescue` pre-PR review was dispatched before opening this PR and
  left running for ~3h against a small, text-only diff with no response; it was
  cancelled and this PR opened without its findings so the independent PR review
  below was not blocked on it.
- Three review rounds from @t-uda (CHANGES_REQUESTED, all addressed and pushed:
  ae369c3 for round 1 — full-build prohibition retracted, `pre-push` description
  corrected, YAML front matter fixed, broken private-contact reference removed;
  2765bee for round 2 — `AGENTS.md` scope clarified, this PR body brought in
  line with actual state, PR template's non-Lean validation bucket narrowed;
  c021727 for round 3 — the same contributor/agent boundary propagated down to
  `docs/guardrails.md`'s Build-first rule and `docs/build-and-checks.md`'s
  "Mandatory build gate" description, and the "no build" vs. "no verification
  needed" conflation for docs/template changes corrected in `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  and the PR template) and two `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` findings (both
  fixed and threads resolved: quoting fix, `pre-push` description fix).
