body:
Refs #152

**Update after @t-uda's review (2026-07-17 21:50 UTC):** changed from `Closes` to `Refs`.
The two structural acceptance-criteria bullets this PR set out to fix (unlimited → finite,
file-scope → declaration-local) are done and build-verified. The other two bullets
("残すものには測定値と理由をコメント" and the release-host wall-clock/memory record) are
**not** fully done — see the "AC status" section below and the full inventory posted at
https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/issues/152#issuecomment-5007888045. Issue #152 stays
open to track that remaining work; this PR is the first, build-verified increment.

## Scope

Audit of every `maxHeartbeats` / `synthInstance.maxHeartbeats` override in `LerayHopf/`
(45 lines across 16 files). Per issue #152's own P2/post-release-ok guidance, this PR
prioritizes the two structural acceptance criteria that are cheap to fix correctly
(unlimited → finite, file-scope → declaration-local) and verifies each change with a
**targeted** `lake build` (never a full build, per the OOM constraint on this host —
container cgroup ~3.42GiB, full build peak ~3.40GiB). It does **not** attempt to
minimize already-finite, already-declaration-local overrides below their current
values — that would require per-declaration binary-search rebuilds, which the issue
explicitly asks to avoid ("時間のかかる縮小実験に深入りしすぎない").

## Changes (all verified by targeted build; static guards all green)

| File | Declaration(s) | Before | After | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean` | file-wide (was applied to all 58 decls) | `synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1000000` / `maxHeartbeats 4000000` (file-scope) | **removed entirely** | `lake build LerayHopf.Torus.ConvectionExtension` clean under defaults, 6m9s |
| `R3/ConvectionExtension.lean` | file-wide (was applied to all 67 decls) | same values, file-scope | **narrowed to 9 decls**: `convBLT_fixedTest_add_w`, `convBLT_fixedTest_smul_w`, `convBLTspan_eq_fixedTest`, `convBLTspan_eH1_span`, `convBLTspan_overlap`, `convFormL2_antisymm`, `detExtend_on_edgeSlot3`, `convFormL2_extends`, `convFormL2_cont_fixedTest` — same values, declaration-local | Removed file-scope override, rebuilt with defaults → exactly these 9 hit `(deterministic) timeout at isDefEq/whnf, maximum number of heartbeats (200000)`; restored as declaration-local `set_option ... in` on just those 9; full module rebuild clean, 8m20s |
| `Torus/EnergyConvection.lean` | `mFourierCoeff3_add`, `mFourierCoeff3_smul_eq`, `mFourierCoeff3_norm_add_le`, `mFourierCoeff3_norm_smul`, `memH1VF_add`, `memH1VF_smul` (6 decls) | `maxHeartbeats 0` (**unlimited**) | `maxHeartbeats 4000000` (finite) | `lake build LerayHopf.Torus.EnergyConvection` clean, 3m3s |

No proof bodies, theorem statements, or signatures were touched — `set_option` value/scope
only.

## AC status (issue #152) — see the linked issue comment for the full 49-row table

(Plain status list, not GitHub task-list syntax — the remaining items are #152's open
work, not TODOs of this PR, and #152 itself tracks them as checkboxes.)

- **Done.** 全 heartbeat override の file / declaration / 理由を一覧化 — full
  mechanically-generated table (file, declaration name, option, value, status, reason)
  posted at https://github.com/uda-lab/leray-hopf/issues/152#issuecomment-5007888045.
- **Done.** unlimited は可能なら有限上限へ変更 — the only 6 `maxHeartbeats 0` overrides are
  now finite.
- **Done.** 必要な override は declaration-local に限定 — both file-scope overrides are gone.
- **Not done** (remains open on #152) — 残すものには測定値と理由をコメント: not done for 31 of
  49 declaration-local overrides (3 already had an inline reason; 15 changed by this PR carry
  a build-verified reason; the remaining 31 are unchanged, inherited values with no
  per-declaration reason or measured minimal value on record).
- **Partial** (remains open on #152) — release host で wall-clock / memory の概算を記録: wall-clock
  recorded for the 3 touched modules only (see Verification summary below); whole-project
  estimate deferred to the next RC build attestation per the issue's own text.

## Remaining overrides — classified (c): keep as-is (finite, declaration-local, unchanged)

The other ~34 declarations across `Analysis/FourierParseval.lean`, `Galerkin/DissipativeODE.lean`,
`R3/ArzelaAscoliTime.lean`, `R3/AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean` (×4), `R3/ConvectionExtension.lean`
(`convBLTspan_add`/`convBLTspan_smul`, pre-existing), `R3/ConvectionForm.lean` (×5),
`R3/CurlDensity.lean`, `R3/EnergyClassConvection.lean`, `R3/FrechetKolmogorov.lean`,
`R3/GalerkinTimeModulus.lean`, `R3/GoodRepresentative.lean` (×2), `R3/SpacetimePrecompact.lean`,
`Torus/ConvectionExtension.lean` (×6, pre-existing), `Torus/ConvectionForm.lean`,
`Torus/EnergyConvection.lean` (3 remaining, already finite), `Torus/LimitPassage.lean` already
satisfy the two structural criteria: **finite** (800000–1600000) and **declaration-local**
(`set_option ... in` immediately preceding the declaration). Three of them
(`AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean:weakFormNS_limit_passage`, and the file-header comments in
`GalerkinTimeModulus.lean`/`SpacetimePrecompact.lean`) already carry an inline reason. The rest
(31) are left unannotated and unchanged in this pass — adding a genuine per-declaration measured
reason would require the expensive bisection the issue explicitly deprioritizes for this P2
audit. This is explicitly **not** claimed as satisfying the "measured value + reason" AC bullet;
see AC status above and the linked issue comment for the exhaustive per-declaration breakdown.

## A note from this session: docstring/`set_option` ordering pitfall

Discovered while narrowing `R3/ConvectionExtension.lean`: placing a `set_option ... in`
(or a plain `--` comment) **between** a declaration's closing doc-comment `-/` and the
declaration keyword breaks Lean's parser (`unexpected token 'set_option'; expected 'lemma'`).
The working order is `set_option ... in` **then** the docstring **then** the declaration —
matches the pre-existing pattern already used elsewhere in this file
(`convBLTspan_add`/`convBLTspan_smul`) and in `AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean:1215`. All 9 new
insertions in this PR follow that order; verified by the full targeted rebuild.

## Verification summary

- `flock /tmp/lean-build.lock lake build <module>` for each touched module — no full `lake build` run.
- 7 static guards: `check-no-sorry`, `check-no-axiom`, `check-theorem-names`, `check-axioms`,
  `check-release-cone`, `test-check-release-cone`, `check-statement-cards` — all green.
- No OOM observed (host had ~1.1–1.2GiB available going in; recovered after each build).
- Codex pre-review (via `codex:codex-rescue`) completed before opening this PR: no blockers,
  no should-fix; one nit (comment wording) addressed in a follow-up commit.
- Codex PR review (top-level comment): "Didn't find any major issues." Recorded as a
  `Reviewed-by: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` artifact comment on this PR.

body:
Closes #151

## What

`scripts/check-release-cone.sh` (issue #147) already enforced that the transitive
import closure of `LerayHopf.lean` — the `import LerayHopf` release surface — is
free of `sorry`, with no `ALLOW_SORRY` escape. It had no equivalent guarantee for
axioms or for placeholder-style incomplete work, which was the actual gap named in
#151's acceptance criteria. This PR extends the same cone-walk (computed once, no
`lake env`, pure static text scan) to also fail, **with no marker escape**, on:

1. **Any `axiom`/`constant`/`opaque`/`unsafe` declaration** in the release cone —
   closes the gap where `check-no-axiom.sh` alone accepts any
   `-- ALLOW_AXIOM:`-marked declaration anywhere in the repo, including inside the
   release cone.
2. **Any declaration under a reserved placeholder namespace**
   (`Scaffold`/`Placeholder`/`Stub`/`Draft`, case-insensitive) — closes the gap
   demonstrated by the historical `Scaffold.exists_lerayHopf_torus3_statement`, a
   bare-Prop placeholder that *was* reachable from `import LerayHopf` before issue
   #144 deleted it outright. A fixed reserved-term name list can't anticipate every
   future placeholder name; banning the namespace class is a structural guard that
   doesn't depend on guessing names in advance.

Also extends `scripts/check-theorem-names.sh`'s reserved-term list with
`statement`/`scaffold` (repo-wide, `ALLOW_NAME`-escapable) as the complementary,
non-cone-scoped guard — this is the guard that would have caught the historical
placeholder's *name* directly, had it existed at the time.

Both new checks currently pass as no-ops: the repo already has zero project axioms
and zero placeholder namespaces anywhere in the release cone (verified by grepping
for actual `axiom`/`opaque`/`unsafe`/`constant` declarations repo-wide — the only
hit is `ExtractNotes.lean`'s `unsafe def main`, which is the extraction-script entry
point, not reachable from `import LerayHopf`). The point of this PR is to make that
already-true guarantee **structural** — enforced going forward — rather than merely
true by inspection today.

## Mapping to #151's acceptance criteria

- [x] release modules の strict allowlist を定義し，project axiom / `sorry` をゼロ要求 —
  `check-release-cone.sh` now enforces both, with no marker escape.
- [x] experimental modules は別 profile — already structurally true since #147
  (`LerayHopf.Experimental` is outside the cone, governed by the ordinary
  `ALLOW_SORRY`/`ALLOW_AXIOM` marker discipline); this PR is what makes the release
  side of that split actually strict rather than sorry-only.
- [x] reserved theorem names と namespace policy を強化 — `statement`/`scaffold`
  added to the reserved-term list; `Scaffold`/`Placeholder`/`Stub`/`Draft`
  namespaces banned outright from the release cone (no escape).
- [x] cheap checks は通常 PR で実行 — already true (`guards` job on `pull_request`);
  unchanged by this PR.
- [x] `#print axioms` live run は manual RC / release 時だけでよい — already true
  (`check-axioms-live.sh` only runs on `workflow_dispatch`); unchanged by this PR.
- [x] full `lake build` を毎 PR / push に復活させない — unchanged; this PR adds no
  build step to the `pull_request` trigger.

## Verification

All six guard scripts, run against the changed tree:

```
$ bash scripts/check-no-sorry.sh
OK: no unmarked 'sorry' in Lean sources.
$ bash scripts/check-no-axiom.sh
OK: no undeclared axiom/constant/opaque/unsafe in Lean sources.
$ bash scripts/check-theorem-names.sh
OK: no overclaiming declaration names in Lean sources.
$ bash scripts/check-axioms.sh
OK: axiom-leak gate passed.
$ bash scripts/check-release-cone.sh
OK: release cone is sorry-free, axiom-free, and free of reserved placeholder
namespaces (92 files transitively imported by LerayHopf.lean).
$ bash scripts/check-statement-cards.sh
OK: statement-card guard passed.
```

Negative tests (each reverted after confirming detection, none committed):

- Injected `axiom fakeTestAxiom_issue151 : True -- ALLOW_AXIOM: ...` into
  `LerayHopf/Core.lean` (in the release cone) → `check-release-cone.sh` correctly
  flagged it despite the `ALLOW_AXIOM` marker.
- Injected `namespace Scaffold … theorem fakeTestPlaceholder_issue151 …` into
  `LerayHopf/Torus/Basic.lean` (in the release cone) → `check-release-cone.sh`
  correctly flagged the namespace.
- Injected `def fakeTest_statement_issue151 : Prop := True` into `LerayHopf/Core.lean`
  → `check-theorem-names.sh` correctly flagged the new `statement` reserved term.

No Lean build was run: the only `.lean` change is a pure docstring/comment update in
`LerayHopf.lean` (module-doc paragraph describing the release-surface guarantee, no
code change), this worktree has no local `.lake` cache to build against, and this
issue's own scope note says it should complete via static guard checks alone — which
it does. The functional change (the two bash scripts) is verified directly above,
positively and negatively.

## Docs kept in sync

`docs/guardrails.md` (two new named rules: No-axiom-in-release-cone,
No-placeholder-namespace-in-release-cone), `docs/build-and-checks.md`,
`docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md`, `LerayHopf.lean`'s module
docstring, and `.github/workflows/lean.yml`'s step names all updated to describe the
extended guarantee.

---

Per the repo's current review policy, this PR awaits the owner's manual review — no
automated reviewer dispatch.
title: guardrail: strengthen release-cone guard with axiom + placeholder-namespace checks (#151)

Closes #168.

## Root cause

The #158-fix commit (2f0fa1d, landed via PR #162) rewrote the relocation note at
`LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolev.lean:520` as a `/-- ... -/` doc comment, but the declaration it
used to attach to (`w1pTime_continuous_in_H`) had already been moved out to
`TimeSobolevExperimental.lean` in that same commit. The next token after the comment is the
Stage D2 `/-! ### ...` module-commentary header, not a declaration — Lean requires a `/--` doc
comment to attach to a following declaration, so this is a parse error:

```
LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolev.lean:530:68 error: unexpected token '/-!'; expected 'lemma'
```

This is exactly the kind of defect static guards (grep-based `sorry`/axiom/name checks) cannot
catch — it's a Lean parser error, only caught by an actual build. Caught by tonight's
stack-tip build at commit `499c952`.

## Fix

One-character-class change: the delimiter goes from `/--` (doc comment, must attach to a
declaration) to `/-!` (standalone module-commentary block, valid on its own). No content
change to the note itself.

## Build validation (green — full build run, per orchestrator authorization)

Ran `lake build LerayHopf.Bochner.TimeSobolev LerayHopf.Bochner.TimeSobolevExperimental LerayHopf.Experimental LerayHopf`:

body:
Closes #166.

## What changed

`ExtractNotes.lean` (the `extract_notes` executable used by the `lean-pde-notes` repo to
build an annotated corpus of declarations) only imported the built `LerayHopf` oleans via
`Lean.importModules #[{ module := \`LerayHopf }] ...`. After #147 (PR #162) split the
sorry-bearing Bochner time-layer modules (`TimeSobolevAC`, `TimeMollification`,
`TimeMollifierInterval`, `TimeSobolevExperimental`) out of root `LerayHopf` into
`LerayHopf.Experimental`, those four modules' declarations would silently drop out of
`extracted/decls.json` on the next notes repin, since the extractor's environment no longer
contained them.

Fix: import both `LerayHopf` and `LerayHopf.Experimental`:
```lean
let env ← Lean.importModules #[{ module := `LerayHopf }, { module := `LerayHopf.Experimental }]
    {} (trustLevel := 1024) (loadExts := true)
```
`isLerayHopfModule` (the filter used everywhere downstream) classifies by the *root* string
component of a module name, so `LerayHopf.Experimental.*` and its transitive imports (e.g.
`LerayHopf.Bochner.TimeSobolevAC`) are already correctly picked up once both roots are in the
import set — no other extractor logic needed. Also updated the file's top module docstring to
describe the two-module coverage.

Owner decision (per the issue): extraction covers root + Experimental, so the annotated corpus
doesn't lose the Bochner time-layer entries.

## Scope / risk

Single file, ~18 lines changed. `ExtractNotes.lean` is a standalone `lean_exe` target
(`lakefile.toml`) that reads *pre-built* oleans at runtime via `Lean.importModules` — it is
NOT source-level imported by any `LerayHopf` module (confirmed: no `import ExtractNotes`
anywhere in the tree), so this diff cannot affect the release cone, any guard script, or
either capstone's axiom/sorry profile.

## Validation (static only)

All 5 guards green (release cone unaffected — same file count as before this change):
```
OK: no unmarked 'sorry' in Lean sources.
OK: no undeclared axiom/constant/opaque/unsafe in Lean sources.
OK: no overclaiming declaration names in Lean sources.
OK: axiom-leak gate passed.
OK: release cone is sorry-free (92 files transitively imported by LerayHopf.lean).
```

No `lake build` run tonight (per policy). The extractor change will be functionally validated
during the `lean-pde-notes` repin extraction itself (`lake exe extract_notes`), per the issue's
acceptance criteria.

## Codex pre-review

Ran locally via the project's codex companion runtime on `git show HEAD` / the diff (read-only,
no lake/lean). No blockers, no should-fix findings: confirmed the `importModules` array syntax
is a straightforward second-element addition matching the pre-existing pattern,
`isLerayHopfModule`'s root-based classification correctly covers `LerayHopf.Experimental.*`,
no stricter fixed-module whitelist exists downstream, the docstring edit is accurate, and
`ExtractNotes` remains unreferenced by any source-level import.

body:
Closes #150.

Stacked on issue-149-lake-metadata / PR #163 (this PR's diff base is that branch; merge order: #163 first, then this).

## What this adds

- `.github/workflows/release-attestation.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow (never push/PR/schedule) that takes an explicit `ref` input (SHA or tag), checks it out, records its `lean-toolchain` content and the sha256 of `lake-manifest.json`, runs a full `lake build` (mathlib-cache-first via `leanprover/lean-action@v1`) plus all 6 discipline guards — `check-no-sorry.sh`, `check-no-axiom.sh`, `check-theorem-names.sh`, `check-axioms.sh`, `check-release-cone.sh`, and the capstone live axiom pin `check-axioms-live.sh` — and writes a structured attestation record (SHA, toolchain, manifest hash, per-step pass/fail, guard-log sha256 checksums) to both the job summary and an uploaded artifact (90-day retention, the GitHub public-repo cap).
- README badge linking to the workflow's runs page, with an explicit caveat that it is **not** an always-green CI badge — it reflects the most recent manual attestation of one exact SHA, not current HEAD.
- `docs/build-and-checks.md` — new "Release-candidate build attestation" section: how to dispatch (`gh workflow run release-attestation.yml -f ref=<sha>`), how to find the latest attested SHA, and a durability caveat recommending a GitHub Release asset for permanent archival past the retention window.

## Why a separate workflow from `lean.yml`'s existing `full-build` job

`.github/workflows/lean.yml` already has a `full-build` job on `workflow_dispatch` that runs an almost-identical build+guards sequence. `release-attestation.yml` deliberately duplicates rather than reuses it because (a) it needs an explicit `ref` input independent of the dispatch-time branch/tag selector, to attest an arbitrary SHA; (b) its meaning must not drift if `lean.yml` changes for unrelated reasons; (c) it produces a persisted structured record, which the routine dispatch does not. This tradeoff (and the resulting maintenance duplication) is called out in both the workflow's header comment and was explicitly reviewed by codex pre-review (see below), which agreed the separation is justified but flagged the duplication as a real correctness-risk surface — worth a maintenance note, addressed in the header comment.

## Validation

Local `lake build` is forbidden in this environment (repo policy #145); the workflow itself only runs on GitHub-hosted runners and was **not** dispatched by this PR (per orchestrator instruction — dispatch happens later against the final agreed SHA). What was run locally:

- All 5 static guard scripts pass on this branch: `check-no-sorry.sh`, `check-no-axiom.sh`, `check-theorem-names.sh`, `check-axioms.sh`, `check-release-cone.sh`.
- Workflow YAML parsed successfully with `yaml.safe_load` (no `actionlint` available in this sandbox; network install of it was blocked).
- One round of `codex:codex-rescue` pre-review against `git diff issue-149-lake-metadata...HEAD`, which found two real blockers, both fixed in a follow-up commit:
  - Pinned `defaults.run.shell: bash` at the job level, since an unqualified `run:` step's default shell is not guaranteed to enable `pipefail`, and every guard step relies on `cmd | tee log` reporting `cmd`'s exit status rather than `tee`'s.
  - `retention-days: 400` exceeded GitHub's 90-day public-repo artifact cap; lowered to 90 and docs updated to match.

## Not in scope for this PR

- Dispatching the workflow against a real release-candidate SHA (the orchestrator will do this once tonight's merge stack settles).
- Automated GitHub Release attachment for permanent archival (documented as a manual follow-up in `docs/build-and-checks.md`).

body:
Closes #147.

## Stacked PR

Stacked on `issue-153-nonvacuity-comments` (PR #161). This PR's diff is best read against
that branch: `git diff issue-153-nonvacuity-comments...issue-147-experimental-split`.
Merge order for tonight's stack: #159 → #160 → #161 → this PR.

## What changed

`import LerayHopf` (the root release surface) used to transitively import 4 Bochner modules
each containing a `sorry`, so the release surface was not sorry-free even though both
capstone theorems (`exists_lerayHopf_torus3`, `exists_lerayHopf_r3`) are proved kernel-only
(no `sorryAx`, zero project axioms). This PR makes `import LerayHopf` genuinely sorry-free
and adds a static CI guard that enforces it.

1. **`w1pTime_continuous_in_H` extracted** from `LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolev.lean` into a
   new `LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolevExperimental.lean` (enclosing namespace + `open` context
   replicated). `TimeSobolev.lean` itself is now sorry-free and **stays in the root closure**,
   because `R3/AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean` and `R3/EnergyWeakLsc.lean` (both in the root
   closure) import it directly for `kineticEnergy_lsc_transfer` — a lemma declared
   structurally after, and independent of, the extracted theorem. Nothing else references
   `w1pTime_continuous_in_H` in code; `Torus/TraceEnergy.lean` already documented it as
   quarantined before this split. **Update:** the theorem was initially copied verbatim
   (generic `{p q} (hpq : 1 ≤ p ∧ 1 ≤ q)`), but review found that signature FALSE — see
   "Soundness fix (issue #158)" below; it is now restricted to `p = q = 2`.
2. **New `LerayHopf/Experimental.lean`** aggregates the four still-incomplete modules
   (`TimeSobolevAC`, `TimeMollification`, `TimeMollifierInterval`, `TimeSobolevExperimental`)
   with a docstring inventory of what's incomplete in each, sourced from their `ALLOW_SORRY`
   comments.
3. **Root `LerayHopf.lean`** no longer imports the three relocated modules (kept
   `TimeSobolev`); its docstring now describes the two-tier surface: `import LerayHopf` =
   complete sorry-free release, `import LerayHopf.Experimental` = explicit opt-in for
   incomplete Bochner work.
4. **New `scripts/check-release-cone.sh`**: a static, lake-free guard. Parses
   `import LerayHopf.*` lines from source text (no `lake env`, no compilation) to compute the
   transitive import closure of `LerayHopf.lean`, then runs the same comment-aware `sorry`
   scanner as `check-no-sorry.sh` over exactly that closure — but with **no `ALLOW_SORRY`
   exemption** (deliberately stricter: a justified sorry is still not allowed in the release
   cone). Wired into both CI jobs in `.github/workflows/lean.yml`.
5. **README** gets a new "Import guide" section (table of import paths and their status);
   `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/pdelib-staging.md`,
   `docs/references/mathlib-api-survey.md`, and `LerayHopf.lean`'s own comments are corrected
   for the new file locations (`docs/scratch/*` intentionally left untouched — internal
   working notes per the README, not curated docs; that's issue #148's scope).

## Import-closure investigation (why TimeSobolev.lean wasn't moved wholesale)

Before implementing, I checked whether any file staying in the root closure imports the 4
target modules (per #145 stack policy). Two files that must stay in the root closure —
`R3/AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean` (imported directly by root) and `R3/EnergyWeakLsc.lean`
(imported transitively via that file) — both import `TimeSobolev.lean` directly, for
`kineticEnergy_lsc_transfer`. So `TimeSobolev.lean` could not simply move to `Experimental`
without leaving `import LerayHopf` still transitively sorry-carrying. Investigating the file's
internal structure showed the boundary was clean: the sole `sorry`
(`w1pTime_continuous_in_H`) is declared *before* `kineticEnergy_lsc_transfer` and is never
referenced by it or by anything else in the codebase in actual code — only in doc-comment
prose — so extracting just that one theorem resolves the conflict without touching anything
load-bearing. `W1pTime`/`GelfandTriple`/`hToVprimeCLM` (which the extracted theorem still
depends on, via importing the slimmed `TimeSobolev.lean`) are used broadly elsewhere in the
root closure and correctly stay put.

## Validation (static only — see note below)

All 5 guards green on `HEAD`:
```
OK: no unmarked 'sorry' in Lean sources.
OK: no undeclared axiom/constant/opaque/unsafe in Lean sources.
OK: no overclaiming declaration names in Lean sources.
OK: axiom-leak gate passed.
OK: release cone is sorry-free (92 files transitively imported by LerayHopf.lean).
```

**Guard-failure demonstration** (per #145 policy — required before merging a new guard):
temporarily re-added `import LerayHopf.Bochner.TimeMollification` to root `LerayHopf.lean`
and reran `check-release-cone.sh`:
```
LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeMollification.lean:196:  sorry -- ALLOW_SORRY: PR-F3 S1 — ...
ERROR: 'sorry' found in the release cone (transitive import closure of LerayHopf.lean).
The release surface (`import LerayHopf`) must be sorry-free. Move the offending
module(s) behind an explicit opt-in import (e.g. LerayHopf.Experimental) instead.
```
exit 1 as expected. Reverted the test edit before committing (it is not part of this diff).

**Build note (no `lake build` run — static validation only, by design tonight):** this
container's `lake build` is disabled per #145's memory policy (the stack's one full build
runs once at the tip). The orchestrator authorized one bounded exception for this specific
split (`TimeSobolev.lean` + `TimeSobolevExperimental.lean` only, guarded by an unmodified-since-
last-green-build check against commit `383341e`). I computed that closure and found
`LerayHopf/EvolutionTriple.lean` (in the closure) was touched since `383341e` — but only by a
pure docstring addition from #146 (`git diff 383341e..HEAD -- LerayHopf/EvolutionTriple.lean`
shows no code change). Per the authorized fallback rule ("skip the build if the closure is
dirtied"), I skipped the live build and relied on static validation plus a codex pre-review
pass (which read the diff, confirmed the extracted theorem's statement/body are unchanged and
its namespace/`open` context correctly replicated, and found no other importer of the four
relocated declarations). **This split will get its first live type-check at tonight's
single stack-tip build and the #150 release-candidate attestation.**

## Soundness fix (issue #158)

Owner review (formal review, `CHANGES_REQUESTED`) on this PR found that the verbatim-copied
`w1pTime_continuous_in_H` signature is **FALSE** at its stated generality: issue #158 gives an
explicit weighted-`ℓ²` counterexample at `p = q = 1` (separate `L¹` integrability of `u` and
`u'` does not make the dual pairing `⟨u', u⟩` integrable, which the Lions–Magenes proof route
needs via Hölder — an `H`-continuous a.e. representative need not exist). Extracting the
declaration to `Experimental` does not make that claim correct, and this PR's own docstrings
had repeated the pre-existing "genuine Lions–Magenes form / statement kept intact" framing
into new locations.

Fixed (commit `2f0fa1d`): `w1pTime_continuous_in_H` is now stated only at `p = q = 2` —
`(W : W1pTime GT 2 2 T uV)`, no generic `p, q` — the only case with an actual proof plan (the
issue #4 spike's Cauchy–Schwarz route on `L²(V') × L²(V)`), per #158's own "safe correction"
recommendation. Pure signature narrowing on a still-`sorry` declaration: no proof content
added or removed, and zero consumers exist anywhere in the codebase, so nothing else could
break. Synchronized every description this PR introduces or touches
(`TimeSobolevExperimental.lean`, `Experimental.lean`, `TimeSobolev.lean`, README, STATUS.md,
architecture.md, pdelib-staging.md, mathlib-api-survey.md) to drop the overclaiming framing and
state the restriction plus the #158 correction. All 5 guards re-confirmed green after the fix.

Issue #158 remains open for its broader scope (the `lean-pde-notes` corpus repin, postmortem,
recurrence-prevention process items) — none of which block this PR's source-level correctness.

## Codex pre-review

Ran locally via the project's codex companion runtime on
`git diff issue-153-nonvacuity-comments...HEAD` (read-only, no lake/lean). No blockers.
Should-fix/nit findings (the fail-closed grep status fix and the stale-doc-reference fixes
listed above) were all addressed in the follow-up commit before opening this PR.

body:
Closes #153

## Summary

Comments/docstrings around `b_galerkin` (Torus and R3 lanes) and the `R3GalerkinScheme.range_schwartz` field claimed the formula pin "genuinely excludes `b = 0`" / "excludes `P = id`" as an established, formally-proven fact. Grepping the repo confirmed no concrete witness theorem exists anywhere (no `galerkinConvection ≠ 0`, no `convIntegralSchwartz ≠ 0` on a specific Schwartz triple, no `P n ≠ id`) — so the claim overstated the scope of the formal guarantee.

Per the owner's binding decision on #153 (option 2: weaken the comments, do not add concrete witness theorems), every hit was reworded from "the pin genuinely excludes b=0/P=id" to: the field pins the value to the canonical formula; non-triviality is **not** separately formalized (no concrete witness theorem is proved in this repository); this is a statement about the scope of the formal guarantee, not about mathematical soundness — the underlying mathematics (convection integral not identically zero, `L²(ℝ³) ⊄ 𝒮(ℝ³)`) is not in doubt, only its Lean formalization status.

**This is a formal-guarantee-scope fix, not a mathematical-soundness issue** — mirroring the issue's closing acceptance item.

## Scope

Cross-searched Torus / R3 / projection lanes and the generic Galerkin layer for the overclaiming pattern ("genuinely excludes", "excludes `b`/`P`", "generically nonzero" used to imply formal proof). Weakened:

- `LerayHopf/R3/SolutionInterfaces.lean` — module docstring, `range_schwartz` field (×2 sites) + summary bullet, `R3NSForms` struct docstring, `b_galerkin` field docstring, `R3NSForms.core` docstring

`README.md` was checked and has no non-vacuity/soundness claims tied to this pattern, so nothing needed reconciling there. `docs/scratch/**` archival notes were left untouched (out of scope; historical planning artifacts, not living claims).

Comment/docstring-only change — no Lean code tokens, identifiers, types, or definitions were altered. Verified via full `git diff` review.

## Validation


All four passed:

No `lake build` was run (comment-only diff; forbidden for this task per instructions).

Also received a comment-only-diff pre-review pass from a codex agent (via `codex:codex-rescue`, git-diff + grep only, no build), which flagged 4 additional sites outside the initial 4 target files (`LerayHopf/Galerkin/Domain.lean`, `LerayHopf/R3/DivergenceFree.lean`, `HANDOFF.md`, `docs/phase-torus-nsforms-removal.md`) carrying the same pattern; all 4 are addressed in this PR.

body:
## Summary

Closes #146. P0 release blocker: the natural-language claims in the public docs (README, HANDOFF, formalization-review-ja) and in the `SolutionInterfaces.lean` docstrings repeatedly overstated what the production `Galerkin.LerayHopfSolution` bundle / `LerayHopfSolutionFull(_R3)` / the two capstones (`exists_lerayHopf_torus3`, `exists_lerayHopf_r3`) actually carry.

Per the issue's "Required decision", this is **option 2**: weaken the documentation to exactly what the current types guarantee. No new Lean theorems were added; no `.lean` semantics changed (docstring-only edits to `.lean` files).

## What was overclaiming, and the fix

- **`u ∈ L²(0,T;H¹_σ)` (literal Bochner space membership).** The `energy_class` field gives a.e.-in-time H¹ membership (`∀ᵐ t, regMem (u t)`) + interval-integrable viscous dissipation — **not** Bochner `MemLp` valued in H¹ as a Banach space, since the separate `u_aestronglyMeasurable` field is strong measurability into the *ambient* L² space, not into H¹. Multiple docs and two `SolutionInterfaces.lean` docstrings (Torus + R3) stated the stronger claim literally; all corrected.
- **`u ∈ C_w([0,T]; L²_σ)` (weak continuity).** Not a field of the public structure — only a one-sided trace at `t → 0⁺` (`initial_trace`) is exposed. `docs/formalization-review-ja.md` §4.2 previously implied the "good representative" is the weakly-continuous version without noting this doesn't survive as a public field; added an explicit note (the internal `Torus/TraceEnergy.lean` construction *does* prove weak continuity as an intermediate lemma, but that property is a definitional non-inclusion of the exported structure, not a proof gap).
- **Separated-variable test formulation.** `WeakFormNS` tests against `ψ(t)·w(x)`, not general space-time test functions `φ(t,x)`. Declared out of scope (neither proved nor assumed) rather than silently implied equivalent — in `LerayHopf/EvolutionTriple.lean`'s docstring and in the README.
- **Stale `energy_ineq` claim.** `Torus/SolutionInterfaces.lean` said the energy inequality "holds for all `t ≥ 0`"; the actual field is scoped to `t ∈ [0,T]` (this was fixed for the T-scoping in a past Codex round but the docstring was never updated). Corrected.
- **Implicit modeling choices** (no external force, finite-`T` input rather than global-in-time, 𝕋³ = unit torus `(AddCircle 1)³` with Fourier convention `e^{2πikx}`) are now stated explicitly in README under "Modeling scope".

## Claims table

Added a "Claims table (issue #146)" section to `README.md` mapping every natural-language mathematical claim to the exact field/theorem that carries it (or explicitly marking it "not a field" where the natural claim is stronger than what's proved). This satisfies the issue's first acceptance criterion.

## Files touched

`README.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `LerayHopf.lean`, `LerayHopf/EvolutionTriple.lean`, `LerayHopf/Torus/SolutionInterfaces.lean`, `LerayHopf/R3/SolutionInterfaces.lean`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `docs/formalization-review-ja.md`. Did not touch `docs/scratch/`, `docs/milestone.md`, `docs/REPORT.md`, or any import structure (out of scope per the dispatch).

## Validation

Docs-only change; no `lake build` run (per project policy — full build is consolidated at release-candidate attestation, and this container is memory-constrained). Ran the four grep-based guard scripts from the wt-146 worktree, all green:
```
bash scripts/check-no-sorry.sh      # OK
bash scripts/check-no-axiom.sh      # OK
bash scripts/check-theorem-names.sh # OK
bash scripts/check-axioms.sh        # OK
```
Also had a `codex:codex-rescue` agent pre-review the diff against the issue's acceptance criteria (including an independent literal re-translation of both capstone theorem signatures into natural language, cross-checked against the new claims table) — no blocking issues; two wording nits addressed in a follow-up commit.

**Stacked on `issue-144-cleanup`** (PR #159, open, not yet merged): this branch was created from `issue-144-cleanup` and this PR's diff currently includes #144's commits. **Review only the diff vs `issue-144-cleanup`** (`git diff issue-144-cleanup...issue-146-solution-claims`); once #159 merges into `main`, this PR's diff will collapse to just the two commits above.

## Test plan

## Summary

Closes #144 (P0 release blocker).

The M1-era scaffold `LerayHopfSolution`/`ExistsLerayHopf` and `LerayHopfNonunique` were structurally vacuous (free `Prop` fields, a permanent `ALLOW_SORRY` target) and risked being mistaken for the real, proof-carrying results — in particular `LerayHopfSolution` collided by name with the production `Galerkin.LerayHopfSolution` consumed by both capstones (`exists_lerayHopf_torus3`, `exists_lerayHopf_r3`). This PR deletes the scaffold outright rather than further refining it, now that the real capstones have long superseded its structural role.

**Commit 1** (`2d07997`, pre-scope cleanup authorized alongside the P0 work): deletes 6 zero-reference declarations — `SpatialField`, `H1Torus`, `lerayProjection`, `lerayProjection_R3`, `AbstractGalerkinData`, `convFormSchwartzWitness`. body:
Parent release umbrellas:

- source: #145
- notes/site: [uda-lab/lean-pde-notes#63](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde-notes/issues/63)

**Priority: P0 — mathematical soundness / release blocker. 公開前に必ず修正する。**

## Summary

`LerayHopf.Bochner.w1pTime_continuous_in_H` は、現在の型の一般性では偽である。これは単なる doc typo ではなく、`sorry` 付き public specification の statement review が失敗し、その後 source docstring、設計文書、notes corpus が同じ誤った前提を相互に追認した事例である。

この issue は以下を一体として扱う。

1. theorem statement の修正
2. notes/site の誤った自然言語主張の修正
3. 発生経緯の postmortem
4. 同種の `sorry` / scaffold theorem に対する再発防止 gate

Target:

- [`LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolev.lean`](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde/blob/0afd65fb971277b290911d099e112e0ac40ab1f0/LerayHopf/Bochner/TimeSobolev.lean#L513-L535)
- notes annotation: [`w1pTime_continuous_in_H.yaml`](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde-notes/blob/d1f48dc0dd3e8276ecd04742e76a255f2f4745e8/corpus/LerayHopf/w1pTime_continuous_in_H.yaml)

## Current false claim

現在の theorem は、概略として次を主張する。

$$
u \in L^p(0,T;V), \qquad u' \in L^q(0,T;V'), \qquad 1 \le p,\ 1 \le q
$$

から、`H` に値を取る連続代表元の存在を結論する。

しかし `1 ≤ p` と `1 ≤ q` は、弱微分を定義する個々の Bochner integrand を有限区間上で可積分に落とすには使える一方、エネルギー恒等式に現れる dual pairing

$$
t \longmapsto \langle u'(t),u(t)\rangle_{V',V}
$$

の可積分性を保証しない。標準的な proof route はこの積に Hölder を用いるため、典型的には共役指数条件、または少なくとも reciprocal exponent に関する compatibility が必要になる。repo で実際に検討・利用された proof spike は `p=q=2` である。

## Explicit counterexample at `p=q=1`

`H = ℓ²` とし、weighted Hilbert triple を標準基底 `eₙ` に対して

$$
\|e_n\|_V = 2^n, \qquad \|e_n\|_H = 1, \qquad \|e_n\|_{V'} = 2^{-n}
$$

となるように取る。0へ集積する互いに素な時間区間上に、方向 `eₙ`、高さ1、幅 `δₙ = 4⁻ⁿ` の三角形 spike `u(t) = φₙ(t)eₙ` を置く。

このとき

$$
\sum_n \|u\|_{L^1(V),n} \lesssim \sum_n 2^n 4^{-n} = \sum_n 2^{-n} < \infty,
$$

また各 spike の全変動は定数なので

$$
\sum_n \|u'\|_{L^1(V'),n} \lesssim \sum_n 2^{-n} < \infty.
$$

従って `u ∈ L¹(0,T;V)` かつ `u' ∈ L¹(0,T;V')` だが、H-ノルム1の peak と H-ノルム0の gap が0へ集積するため、H-連続な a.e. representative は存在しない。各 spike interior では a.e. 一致する二つの連続曲線は everywhere 一致するため、null-set modification でも peak は除けない。

`p=q=1` は現在の `hpq : 1 ≤ p ∧ 1 ≤ q` を満たすので、current statement を直接反証する。

## Safe correction

最小で安全な release fix は、repo の実際の用途と既存 proof spike に合わせて theorem を `W1pTime GT 2 2 T uV` に限定すること。

一般指数版を残す場合は、次を別途行う。

- 文献の exact theorem statement と仮定を edition / theorem number / page 付きで固定
- dual pairing の可積分性を保証する exponent relation を Lean type に明示
- endpoint cases を含む proof または formal reduction
- `p=q=1`、`p=q=2`、`p=1,q=∞` 等の boundary-case review

一般化は proof と同時に行い、未証明の generic public API を先に置かない。

## Timeline / how this happened

### 1. Scaffold specification として導入

[commit `95571d3`](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde/commit/95571d31f1ba45b6fa1aa2d8811652cb32790bf9) で、6ファイル・多数の deferred theorem を含む 4-stream scaffold の一部として導入された。最初から `sorry` であり、`hpq : 1 ≤ p ∧ 1 ≤ q` もこの時点から存在した。

commit message / docstring は `genuine Lions–Magenes form`、`statement kept intact`、`4-round adversarial statement gate approved` と記録している。しかし named theorem の exact exponent hypotheses と照合した証跡はない。

### 2. Nearby statement defects は修正されたが、この theorem は out of scope

同じ `TimeSobolev.lean` 周辺では、その後以下の real statement defects が発見・修正された。

- limit measurability の不足
- non-complete target で Bochner integral が collapse する問題
- `W1pTime.ofHValuedDeriv` における `p,q<1` の integrability 不足

一方 `w1pTime_continuous_in_H` は「months-class residual」「separate frontier」として proof scope 外に置かれた。そのため、近傍で statement-gate が機能した経験が、未監査の本 theorem にも confidence を与えてしまった。

### 3. Proof analysis は `2,2` に特殊化されていた

[issue #4 の Lions–Magenes spike](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde/issues/4#issuecomment-4849449949) が実際に検討したのは `W1pTime GT 2 2 T` である。energy pairing の limit passageも `L²(V') × L²(V)` の Cauchy–Schwarz を使う。

つまり proof plan は正しい特殊ケースに対してのみ成立していたが、public theorem の generic signature は同期して狭められなかった。

### 4. Dead / off-critical-path 判定

[commit `7bb9b27`](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde/commit/7bb9b276e6e17724aeefcdbe9a325b8ab77f830d) で、theorem は repo 内で applied nowhere、capstone critical path 外と判定された。その際にも `true, faithful` と記述され、proof / counterexample review の優先度だけが下がった。

capstone がこの theorem を参照しないため、capstone の kernel-only axiom pin は clean のままであり、false public theorem を検出できない。

### 5. Notes が source の自己評価を増幅

notes [PR #24](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde-notes/pull/24) では、最初は generic generated prose の `tier: full` annotation として追加された。review focus は coverage と generated source artifact だった。

notes [PR #48](https://github.com/uda-lab/lean-pde-notes/pull/48) で handwritten annotation へ格上げされた。Codex review は `W^{1,p}(V)` という誤った空間表記を正しく指摘し、実際の Lean type `u ∈ L^p(V), u' ∈ L^q(V')` に合わせたが、`p,q` compatibility は検査しなかった。

結果として false statement がより忠実かつ自信のある日本語で再掲され、`主張は本来の強さのまま保たれている` とまで書かれた。source と notes は同じ docstring / theorem-name assumption を使っており、独立な二重確認ではなかった。

## Antipatterns

1. **Named-theorem anchoring** — `Lions–Magenes` という名称から familiar `2,2` theorem を頭の中で補い、actual binders を検査しない。
2. **Accidental quantifier inflation** — 必要な `2,2` special case を proof なしで arbitrary `p,q` API に一般化する。
3. **Separate integrability vs pairing integrability confusion** — `u` と `u'` が各々 L¹ であることと、`⟨u',u⟩` が L¹ であることを混同する。
4. **`sorry`-green-build fallacy** — elaboration / full build の成功を statement の真偽確認と混同する。
5. **Honest-sorry ⇒ true-statement fallacy** — 未証明であることを正直に表示したことを、specification の正しさの証拠として扱う。
6. **Special-case proof / general API mismatch** — proof spike は `2,2` なのに public signature は generic のまま。
7. **Dead theorem rot** — consumer がないため proof priority は下がるが、public namespace / scholarly site では主張として残る。
8. **Self-referential verification** — notes が誤った source docstring を authority とし、source/notes が互いを確認したように見える。
9. **Large-batch review dilution** — 多数の scaffold / 61 annotations の batch review で theorem-level literature matching が希薄化する。
10. **AI consensus without epistemic independence** — implementation、statement gate、notes review が既存の confidence prose を共有し、独立に counterexample search しない。
11. **Claim laundering** — `genuine`、`faithful`、`gate-approved`、`true` という工程上の文言が繰り返され、数学的証拠の代わりになる。

## Required fixes

### Theorem / source

- [ ] current generic theorem を release surface から除去または正しい statement に変更
- [ ] 最小 fix として `p=q=2` specialization を検討
- [ ] generic version を残す場合は exact exponent compatibility と文献を明示
- [ ] docstring / `STATUS.md` / architecture / pdelib staging の `true` / `faithful` / `statement intact` claims を修正
- [ ] obsolete reflection / mollification design commentsを corrected theorem scope に同期
- [ ] public `sorry` / scaffold theorem の axiom profile を release tooling で可視化

### Notes / site

- [ ] annotation を false claim として quarantine し、修正 source PIN へ repin
- [ ] `tier: full` と `proof_status` を分離
- [ ] `contains-sorry` / `invalid-statement` / `retired` 等を UI で明示
- [ ] natural-language statement に Lean hypotheses を省略せず掲載
- [ ] literature citation と exact theorem conditions を付与

### Process / recurrence prevention

- [ ] public `sorry` theorem ごとに statement card を導入: exact type、reference、hypothesis mapping、consumer special case、boundary cases
- [ ] exponent-parametric theorem に adversarial substitutions を必須化
- [ ] weighted `ℓ²` / spike / noncomplete / nonmeasurable counterexample checklist を statement gate に追加
- [ ] proof plan が special case の場合、public theorem もその case に限定
- [ ] elaboration gate、capstone axiom gate、public API semantic gate を別々に報告
- [ ] 少なくとも一人は prior confidence prose を読まない blind statement review を行う
- [ ] large annotation batch の coverage review と mathematical review を分離

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] source theorem no longer admits the `p=q=1` counterexample
- [ ] corrected theorem is proved、または明示的 experimental/scaffold namespace と proof status を持つ
- [ ] source docs / notes prose / site UI が corrected exact statement と一致
- [ ] source and notes release umbrellas が本 issue を P0 として追跡
- [ ] regression guard が current over-general signature の再導入を検出
- [ ] postmortem と recurrence checklist が contributor-facing documentation に残る

## CI note

この修正の statement / corpus / provenance checks は軽量 gate で行う。full `lake build` は毎 push ではなく、release-candidate exact SHA の低頻度 attestation にまとめる。
title: [P0][soundness][postmortem] `w1pTime_continuous_in_H` の偽な一般化を修正し statement-gate を再設計する

Parent: #145

**Priority: P0 — release blocker. 公開前に必ず完了する．**

## 問題

本番用 `Galerkin.LerayHopfSolution` は，弱形式，エネルギー不等式，初期 trace，a.e. の正則性所属，散逸量の可積分性，L² 値写像としての強可測性を持つ．一方，README・HANDOFF・formalization review はこれをしばしば標準的な

- `u ∈ L²(0,T;H¹_σ)`
- `u ∈ C_w([0,T];L²_σ)`
- 「完全な Leray–Hopf 解」

として翻訳している．前者の H¹ 値 Bochner `MemLp` と後者の弱連続性は，現在の最終 public structure が直接保持する field ではない．

また，`WeakFormNS` は分離変数 test `ψ(t)w(x)` による formulation で，integrand の可積分性 field を自体には持たない．方程式は外力なしである．

## Required decision

各項目について次のどちらかを選び，型と説明を一致させる：

1. conventional な内容を theorem / field として導出・公開する．
2. 公開文書の主張を，現在の型が直接保証する「a.e. H¹-membership + integrable dissipation」等へ厳密に弱める．

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 公開 README に，solution bundle の各数学的主張と対応する field / theorem の表がある
- [ ] `L²_t H¹_x` について，Bochner membership theorem を公開するか，その literal claim を文書から外す
- [ ] 弱連続性 `C_w([0,T];L²_σ)` を公開するか，本 repo の定義選択として非包含を明記
- [ ] 分離変数 test formulation と標準 space-time test formulation の関係を証明または scope として明記
- [ ] full solution の弱形式 integrand の可積分性を theorem として package するか，必要仮定を明記
- [ ] 外力なし，時間区間，unit torus の正規化を明記
- [ ] capstone docstring と日本語・英語 prose が Lean statement より強いことを言っていない
- [ ] 変更後の主要 theorem statements は review で再度自然言語へ逐語的に翻訳して照合
title: [P0][release-blocker] 公開する Leray–Hopf 解の型と自然言語上の主張を一致させる

body:
## Summary

Issue #135 asked to narrow the `GalerkinSolutionData_R3` hypothesis to the
generic `Galerkin.SolutionData` bundle in 8 declarations, on the premise that
all 8 consume only generic fields (`.u`/`.u_hasDeriv`/`.u_ode`/`.energy_bound`)
and never `viscous_curve_continuous`.

Before editing, I traced the call graph for all 8 targets. The direct-field-use
premise holds (none of the 8 reference `viscous_curve_continuous` by name in
their own body), but 5 of the 8 have a **transitive** dependency that blocks
narrowing without either new mathematical work or touching structures the
issue explicitly rules out of scope. This PR narrows the 3 declarations that
are genuinely clean and documents the blocker evidence for the other 5, per
the issue's own stopping rule ("scope it per-declaration and stop where it is
not cheap").

## Narrowed (3)

| Declaration | File |
|---|---|
| `galerkin_weakLimit_R3` | `LerayHopf/R3/ArzelaAscoliTime.lean` |
| `perTest_hasDerivAt_R3` (private) | `LerayHopf/R3/GoodRepresentative.lean` |
| `perTest_lipschitz_R3` | `LerayHopf/R3/GoodRepresentative.lean` |

Each now takes `galSeq : ∀ n, Galerkin.SolutionData (r3Domain 𝔊) F.core ν u₀ n`
instead of `∀ n, GalerkinSolutionData_R3 𝔊 F ν u₀ n`. Call sites that hold
concrete `GalerkinSolutionData_R3` data (inside `u_lim_aestronglyMeasurable`
and `exists_weak_representative_R3`, both still concrete — see below) project
down via `.toSolutionData`.

`perTest_lipschitz_R3` needed one additional local helper,
`galerkin_norm_le_u0_generic` (private, `GoodRepresentative.lean`) — a verbatim
port of `EnergyWeakLsc.galerkin_norm_le_u0`'s already-proven statement, retyped
onto the generic bundle. The concrete lemma can't be reused directly: it's
typed on `GalerkinSolutionData_R3`, and there's no `GalerkinSolutionData_R3 →
Galerkin.SolutionData` projection to go the other way. Both proofs are
byte-identical in reasoning (only the binder type differs); this stays
`private` and local to avoid rippling into `galerkin_norm_le_u0`'s ~15 other
call sites across unrelated files.

## Blocked (5) — not narrowed, with evidence

1. **`galerkin_spacetime_precompact_R3`** (`ArzelaAscoliTime.lean` ~L135) — its
   entire body is a one-line delegation to
   `galerkin_spacetime_precompact_of_goodSampling` in
   `LerayHopf/R3/SpacetimePrecompact.lean` (not a target, upstream/imported,
   "byte-identical statement" by design). That callee's proof runs through
   `galerkin_sampling_error_bound` (D3, `GalerkinTimeModulus.lean:535`), which
   at line 592 calls `galerkin_viscous_curve_continuousOn gs` — i.e. it
   genuinely consumes `gs.viscous_curve_continuous`
   (`GalerkinTimeModulus.lean:103` too). This is the H¹/Dirichlet-energy
   mesh-sampling bound (Steklov–Jensen good-sample selection) the local
   Aubin–Lions–Simon compactness argument is actually built on — load-bearing
   math, not a spurious interface requirement. Narrowing the target's binder
   without narrowing the whole D2/D3 chain makes the one-line delegation
   ill-typed; narrowing the chain too would mean re-deriving the
   sampling-error bound without H¹ continuity, i.e. new math.
2. **`perBall_ae_subseq`** (~L778) — calls `galerkin_spacetime_precompact_R3`
   directly with the same `galSeq` binder; inherits the block.
3. **`diag_ae_subseq`** (~L834) — calls `perBall_ae_subseq`; inherits the block.
4. **`u_lim_aestronglyMeasurable`** (~L935) — calls `diag_ae_subseq`; inherits
   the block. (It also calls the now-narrowed `galerkin_weakLimit_R3`, fine on
   its own, via the `.toSolutionData` projection in this PR — but that doesn't
   rescue the whole declaration.)
5. **`exists_weak_representative_R3`** (`GoodRepresentative.lean` ~L169) —
   takes `alPkg : AubinLionsPackage_R3 𝔊 F ν T u₀ galSeq` as a hypothesis.
   `AubinLionsPackage_R3` (`SolutionInterfaces.lean:533-535`) is itself
   parameterized by the concrete `∀ n, GalerkinSolutionData_R3 𝔊 F ν u₀ n`.
   `AubinLionsPackage_R3` is out of scope per the issue's own ruling b ("no
   unification"). Narrowing this target's own `galSeq` binder would make the
   `alPkg` hypothesis ill-typed without touching `AubinLionsPackage_R3`, which
   is forbidden. It also calls `kineticEnergy_lsc_bound`
   (`EnergyWeakLsc.lean:121-124`), likewise `AubinLionsPackage_R3`-locked.

**Census correction:** the original premise (both files consume
`viscous_curve_continuous` directly) doesn't hold — direct field use inside
the 8 target bodies is zero. The real binding is transitive, via the D3
sampling-error-bound chain, and only affects the
precompact/subsequence-extraction family plus the `AubinLionsPackage_R3`-typed
target.

## Verification

- `flock lake build` (incremental, serialized): exit 0, `Build completed
  successfully (3196 jobs)`.
- `scripts/check-no-sorry.sh`, `scripts/check-no-axiom.sh`,
  `scripts/check-theorem-names.sh`: all `OK`.
- `scripts/agent-preflight.sh`: `PREFLIGHT OK`, including
  `scripts/check-axioms.sh` and the live `#print axioms` pin —
  `exists_lerayHopf_torus3` and `exists_lerayHopf_r3` both still
  `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` (kernel-only, unchanged).
- `git diff main -- LerayHopf/Torus/GalerkinODECapstone.lean
  LerayHopf/R3/GalerkinODECapstone.lean LerayHopf/R3Capstone.lean`: **empty** —
  neither capstone was touched at all.
- No new `sorry`, no new `axiom`/`opaque`/`unsafe`, no theorem renamed, no
  statement weakened.

Closes #135.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <<email-redacted>>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WG2AUxk5fQfZqndYeJ1Xjb

## Summary

Addresses finding 6 of #1 (componentwise-lemma dedup). The Fin-3 reassembly lemma and
the real-part round-trip lemma for `L2VF_projComponent`/`L2VF_injectComponent` were
each re-derived independently at multiple sites instead of being shared. This PR
promotes both to public theorems next to the operators they describe in
`LerayHopf/Torus/DivergenceFree.lean` and rewires all three consumers to call them.

## New public lemma names (in `DivergenceFree.lean`, next to `L2VF_projComponent`/`L2VF_injectComponent`)

- `re_compLpL_projComponentC (j : Fin 3) (w : L2VF)` — taking the real part undoes the
  complex embedding of a component: `reCLM.compLpL 2 haarTorus3 (L2VF_projComponentC j w) = L2VF_projComponent j w`.
- `sum_inject_projComponent (w : L2VF)` — the Fin-3 reassembly: `∑ j, L2VF_injectComponent j (L2VF_projComponent j w) = w`.
- `injectComponent_projComponent_ae (j : Fin 3) (w : L2VF)` (private) — the shared
  a.e.-pointwise helper factoring out the identical `filter_upwards` proof used by
  `sum_inject_projComponent`.

## 3-site rewire table

| Site | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `H1Sigma.lean:108–151` | private `re_compLpL_projComponentC` + private `sum_inject_projComponent` (full re-proof) | deleted; call sites (lines ~212, ~217) resolve unchanged to the new public originals (same `namespace LerayHopf`, transitively imported via `Leray.lean → DivergenceFree.lean`) |
| `VelocityGalerkin.lean:338–377` (inline `have hre` / `have hcomp` / `have hdecomp` inside `velocityProjection_n_tendsto`) | ~40 lines of inline re-derivation | `have hre := fun j => re_compLpL_projComponentC j u`; `have hdecomp := sum_inject_projComponent u` |
| `GalerkinScheme.lean:96–121` (inline `have hreassemble` inside `L2VF_ext_componentC_mFourierCoeff`) | ~26 lines of inline re-derivation | direct calls `sum_inject_projComponent u` / `sum_inject_projComponent v` in the closing `calc` |

Import direction verified before editing: all three consumers already transitively
import `LerayHopf.Torus.DivergenceFree` (`H1Sigma.lean → Leray.lean → DivergenceFree.lean`;
`VelocityGalerkin.lean → Leray.lean → DivergenceFree.lean`; `GalerkinScheme.lean → SolutionInterfaces.lean → {Leray.lean, VelocityGalerkin.lean}`) — no new imports needed, no cycle risk.

## Scope

No statement changes to any existing public declaration, no renames, no relocation of
anything else, no other files touched (besides the untracked pre-existing
`docs/scratch/PROJECT-SUMMARY-ARTIFACT.md`, which is out of scope and untouched).

Net LOC: **+64/−113** across 4 files.

## Build / preflight evidence

- Incremental `lake build` (serialized under `flock`): green, 3196/3196 jobs. All four
  touched files built successfully: `LerayHopf.Torus.DivergenceFree`,
  `LerayHopf.Torus.H1Sigma`, `LerayHopf.Torus.VelocityGalerkin`,
  `LerayHopf.Torus.GalerkinScheme` (only pre-existing unrelated warnings elsewhere).
- `check-no-sorry.sh` / `check-no-axiom.sh` / `check-theorem-names.sh`: all PASS.
- `bash scripts/agent-preflight.sh`: PREFLIGHT OK, including the live axiom pin —
  both capstones remain kernel-only:
  ```
  'LerayHopf.exists_lerayHopf_torus3' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
  'LerayHopf.exists_lerayHopf_r3' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
  AXIOM LIVE PIN OK — all 4 declarations match their pinned axiom sets (R3: 0 project axioms — KERNEL-ONLY, 𝕋³: 0 project axioms — KERNEL-ONLY)
  ```
- Pre-push hook (grep guards + serialized incremental build): green on push.
- Remaining `sorry` count: unchanged (this PR touches only fully-proved lemmas).
- New assumptions: none.

Addresses finding 6 of #1

## Summary

`LerayHopf/Torus/TraceEnergy.lean` carried five `private` near-verbatim duplicates
of the public generics in `LerayHopf/Bochner/WeakLimitToolkit.lean` — left over from
the extraction that originally built the domain-neutral toolkit (whose own
provenance header already said "five lemmas extracted verbatim from
`LerayHopf.Torus.TraceEnergy`"). This PR rewires TraceEnergy to import the toolkit
and call the public originals directly, deleting the five private copies.

## Statement-correspondence table

Verified via a scripted diff of each theorem's signature (name through `:= by`),
stripping only the `private` modifier — all five are **byte-identical**:

| Private copy (TraceEnergy.lean, before) | Toolkit original (WeakLimitToolkit.lean) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `normSq_le_liminf_of_inner_tendsto` — line 275 | line 49 | IDENTICAL |
| `cauchySeq_inner_extend` — line 338 | line 112 | IDENTICAL |
| `exists_weak_limit_in_submodule` — line 386 | line 160 | IDENTICAL |
| `exists_mem_of_ae_full` — line 458 | line 232 | IDENTICAL |
| `cauchySeq_of_equiLipschitz_of_dense` — line 498 | line 272 | IDENTICAL |

(Issue #131 named the first four; the fifth, `normSq_le_liminf_of_inner_tendsto`, has
the same staleness and was in scope per the task instructions.)

## Changes

- `LerayHopf/Torus/TraceEnergy.lean`: added `import LerayHopf.Bochner.WeakLimitToolkit`;
  deleted the `section HilbertToolkit … end HilbertToolkit` block (lemmas 1–3, plus its
  `variable {E …}` line, now unused) and the two standalone private lemmas 4–5. Call sites
  (5 of them) resolve unchanged to the toolkit originals since both files share
  `namespace LerayHopf`. No statement changes, no renames, no other file touched.
- `LerayHopf/Bochner/WeakLimitToolkit.lean`: updated only the Provenance doc-comment
  to record that issue #131 rewired TraceEnergy to these originals and the private
  copies are gone. No code changes.

Net: **-275 LOC** in TraceEnergy.lean (1483 → 1208 lines), `+4/-3` in the toolkit's
doc-comment. `energyBudget_liminf_assembly` and `schwartz_trilinear_bound_L326_energy`
relocation is explicitly out of scope and untouched.

## Build / preflight evidence

- Incremental `lake build` (serialized under `flock`): **green**, 3196/3196 jobs,
  `Built LerayHopf.Bochner.WeakLimitToolkit` and `Built LerayHopf.Torus.TraceEnergy`
  both succeed (only pre-existing unrelated warnings elsewhere in the tree).
- `check-no-sorry.sh` / `check-no-axiom.sh` / `check-theorem-names.sh`: all **PASS**.
- `bash scripts/agent-preflight.sh`: **PREFLIGHT OK**, including the live axiom pin —

  ```
  'LerayHopf.exists_lerayHopf_r3' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
  ```

body:
## Summary

`flock(1)` is util-linux and does not exist on macOS, so enabling the documented hook (`git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks`) blocked **every** push on darwin with `flock: command not found` (#118).

Final design (after two codex adversarial passes) — `run_build_locked()` with three tiers:

1. **Linux (unchanged)**: `flock /tmp/lean-build.lock lake build` — byte-identical to the previous behavior; the existing serialization on the 3.42 GiB shared container is preserved.
2. **darwin fallback**: a perl one-liner takes the **same kernel `flock(2)`** (`LOCK_EX`, blocking) on the same `/tmp/lean-build.lock`, clears `FD_CLOEXEC` (`fcntl(F_SETFD, 0)` — load-bearing: perl sets close-on-exec on fds above `$^F`, which would silently release the lock at exec; the stress harness caught exactly that as 5/6 overlapping builds), then `exec`s `lake build` so the lock fd lives exactly as long as the build. `/usr/bin/perl` ships with macOS. **No lock files to reclaim, no stale/pidless/PID-reuse states, no cleanup traps** — the earlier mkdir-protocol drafts (e587868, 10a5143) had reclaim races in exactly those states (both codex passes each caught one) and were deleted wholesale in favor of the kernel primitive, per the pass-2 recommendation.
3. **Neither flock nor perl**: warn (at the call site, so the `$LOG` redirect can't swallow it) and build unserialized — mirrors the existing `scripts/agent-preflight.sh` precedent.

## Report (per AGENTS.md)

- **Files changed**: `scripts/hooks/pre-push` only. No Lean sources touched.
- **Theorem/def names added**: none. **Remaining `sorry`**: unchanged (guards green). **New assumptions**: none.
- **Build**: `bash scripts/agent-preflight.sh` green — `PREFLIGHT OK`, live axiom pin OK (both capstones kernel-only).

## Verification

- `bash -n` clean.
- Functional tests via a flock-free symlink-farm `PATH` with stub `lake` binaries, feeding the hook real ref lines on stdin (range contains `.lean` changes so the build branch triggers):
  1. **6-way parallel stress** on the perl path with a mutual-exclusion-checking stub — 6/6 exit 0, **zero critical-section overlaps**, no leftover lock state;
  2. **cross-tool mutual exclusion**: the perl path blocks behind a live util-linux `flock` holder on the same file (still waiting at 45 s), proceeds after release — proves both tiers contend on the same kernel lock;
  3. build failure propagates through `exec` and still blocks the push with the log tail;
  4. warning tier visible on console; flock-branch regression green.

Closes #118

Part of the issue #112 GalerkinDomain campaign (PR-C; PR-A #132 and PR-B #133 merged). Introduces the domain-neutral bundle layer and routes both lanes through it as instances.

## Files changed (10)
- **NEW** `LerayHopf/Galerkin/Domain.lean` — `Galerkin.Domain` (ambient space, div-free subspace, projector family, domain functionals), `NSFormCore` (domain-neutral convection form), `Domain.evolution`.
- **NEW** `LerayHopf/Galerkin/SolutionBundles.lean` — `SolutionData`, `LerayHopfSolution`, `CompactnessPackage`, `exists_lerayHopf_from_package`.
- `LerayHopf.lean` — +2 imports for the new layer.
- `LerayHopf/Torus/SolutionInterfaces.lean` — `torusDomain`, `Torus3NSForms.core`, reduction lemmas; `torus3Evolution`/`GalerkinSolutionData`/`LerayHopfSolutionFull`/`GalerkinCompactnessPackageFull` become abbrevs; assembly delegates.
- `LerayHopf/R3/SolutionInterfaces.lean` — `r3Domain 𝔊`, `R3NSForms.core`, reduction lemmas; `r3Evolution` abbrev; `GalerkinSolutionData_R3` now `extends Galerkin.SolutionData` + its R3-specific `viscous_curve_continuous`; Full bundles become abbrevs; assembly delegates.
- 6 downstream mechanical fixups: `R3/{AubinLionsLimitPassage,GalerkinCurveBounds,GalerkinTrilinearBound,GoodRepresentative}.lean`, `Torus/{ModeCompactness,TraceEnergy}.lean`.

## Declarations added
`Galerkin.{Domain, NSFormCore, Domain.evolution, SolutionData, LerayHopfSolution, CompactnessPackage, exists_lerayHopf_from_package}`; `torusDomain`, `Torus3NSForms.core`, `r3Domain`, `R3NSForms.core`; `rfl` projection-reduction lemmas `{torusDomain,r3Domain}_{stokes,dissip,regMem,regIntegrand}` and `{Torus3NSForms,R3NSForms}.core_b`.

Field NAMES and all public statements are unchanged; both lanes recover their current structures definitionally (`F.core.b ≡ F.b`, `torusDomain.stokes ≡ stokesTestPairing`, etc.). Per-lane `AubinLionsPackage[_R3]` left untouched (ruling b — global-vs-local Rellich divergence is mathematics, not duplication).

### Two annotations worth calling out
- **`Domain.σ_complete : CompleteSpace ↥σ` field** — `CompleteSpace ↥D.σ` is not inferable for an abstract submodule (it is closed, but that is not derivable from `CompleteSpace X`); carried as data, discharged by `inferInstance` from the existing `CompleteSpace L2Sigma`/`L2Sigma_R3` instances. Anticipated by plan §3.4.
- **`@[reducible]` on `torusDomain`/`r3Domain`/`Domain.evolution`** — required for (a) subtype→ambient coercions in the per-lane bundle fields and (b) keeping `WeakFormNS (evolution)` unfolding on the reducible fast path; a non-reducible `Domain.evolution` caused a mixed-transparency whnf blowup (timed out even at 1M heartbeats), so reducibility restores the pre-refactor behavior.

## Transparency note on the assembly proof
The generic `exists_lerayHopf_from_package` is a trivial 6-field repackaging identical to the former per-lane `exists_lerayHopf_from_package_full[_R3]` proofs. It was planned as a coder `sorry` scaffold for the prover, but discharging it inline was necessary to keep the capstones kernel-only (routing them through a `sorry` would have introduced `sorryAx`). Flagging transparently that this proof-body work rode in the coder pass.

## Reports
- **Remaining `sorry` in touched files: 0.** New axioms: none.
- **Preflight green** (`lake build LerayHopf` 3198 jobs; check-no-sorry/axiom/theorem-names; static + live `#print axioms` gates).
- **Both capstones KERNEL-ONLY**: `exists_lerayHopf_torus3` and `exists_lerayHopf_r3` = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. Capstone files show an empty diff (statements byte-identical).
- **Codex xhigh audit clean**: zero field-level statement drift, no `regIntegrand`/`regBoundRHS` cross-contamination, no assembly-field loss; its only finding was that its sandbox cannot run Lake, satisfied by the local preflight above.

## Summary

PR-B of the issue #112 campaign (`docs/scratch/galerkin-domain-plan.md`, architect-frozen
plan §3.3): instantiates the generic `LerayHopf.Galerkin.FieldForms` layer (landed in PR-A,
#132) on both lanes, bridges each lane's concrete `galerkinODE_vectorField` to the generic
construction, converts every downstream lane theorem into a byte-identical corollary of that
bridge, and deletes the now-dead locally-duplicated CLM tower and tiling/gluing machinery that
those corollaries superseded.

## Files changed (4)

- `LerayHopf/Torus/GalerkinODESolve.lean`
- `LerayHopf/R3/GalerkinODEExistence.lean`
- `LerayHopf/R3/GalerkinODESolve.lean`
- `LerayHopf/R3/GalerkinODE.lean`

- `torusFieldForms` (`Torus/GalerkinODESolve.lean`) — the `Galerkin.FieldForms (velocitySpan n)`
  witness for the torus lane; all 13 structure obligations proved.
- `r3FieldForms` (`R3/GalerkinODEExistence.lean`) — the `Galerkin.FieldForms (galerkinSpan B n)`
  witness for the ℝ³ lane; all 13 structure obligations proved.
- `galerkinODE_vectorField_eq_generic` (both lanes) — the equality bridge: the lane's concrete
  vector field equals the generic `FieldForms.vectorField`, proved by `ext_inner_right` + both
  specs per the plan's equality-bridge rule.
- `hasDerivAt_intrinsic_of_coe` (private, both lanes) — reflects an ambient `HasDerivAt` back to
  the intrinsic curve, letting the corollaries below feed the generic `Galerkin` lemmas.
- `stokesTestPairing_R3_symm` — promoted from a `private` copy in `R3/GalerkinODESolve.lean` to a
  public theorem in `R3/GalerkinODE.lean` (proof body moved verbatim), breaking an import-cycle
  blocker so `r3FieldForms` could cite it directly instead of needing a scaffold.

## Declarations deleted (dead code, zero external consumers verified by repo-wide grep)

- Both lanes: `rieszSymmCLM`(`_apply`), `bInner`(`_apply`), `bMid`(`_apply`), `bOut`(`_apply`),
  `galerkinODE_bilinearPart`(`_apply`), `stokesInner`(`_apply`), `stokesOut`(`_apply`),
  `galerkinODE_linearPart`(`_apply`), `galerkinODE_vectorField_eq_parts` (the full CLM tower),
  `solve_hasDerivAt_ambient`, `solve_exists_on_step` (the tiling/gluing helpers).
- R3 only: `stokesInner_add`, `stokesInner_smul` (private helpers used solely inside the deleted
  `stokesOut`).

`galerkinODE_bilinearPart`/`galerkinODE_linearPart` were the only public names among the
deleted set; their deletion was explicitly sanctioned by plan §3.3/§1.

## Lane theorems converted to corollaries (statements byte-identical, unchanged)

Both lanes' `galerkinODE_vectorField_contDiff` (C1), `galerkinField_inner_self_nonpos` (A1),
`energy_hasDerivAt_of_localSolution`/`galerkinField_uniform_local_time`/
`galerkinField_solution_agree` (A2/G1 helpers), `norm_le_of_forwardSolution` (A3), and
`forwardGlobalSolution_exists` (G1) — 12 theorems total — now derive their content from
`LerayHopf.Galerkin.{DissipativeODE,QuadraticField}` via the equality bridge, instead of a
locally-duplicated proof route. No statement of any of these 12, the torus reg-payoff tail, the
torus-hosted public Fourier lemmas (`velocityProjection_n_norm_le`,
`L2VF_norm_sq_eq_sum_componentC`, `h1EnergySq_eq_L2_add_viscous`, `galerkinCurve_reg_mem`, the
`stokesTestPairing_*` B.0 family), or the three lane deliverables (`galerkinSolutionData_torus`,
`finDimGlobalODE_exists`, `galerkinSolutionData_unconditional`) was touched — confirmed by diff

Also fixed a stale module docstring in `R3/GalerkinODESolve.lean` that falsely claimed
"ALLOW_SORRY scaffold placeholders below" (the file is now sorry-free) and rewrote the "HONEST
scope"/"Import justification" sections to describe the new witness+bridge+corollary structure.

## Net effect

`git diff --stat main...HEAD`: 4 files changed, 315 insertions(+), 1101 deletions(-),
**net −786 lines**.

- Remaining `sorry`: **0** in the four touched files. Repo-wide count unchanged: 5 pre-existing

- New axioms: **none**.
- `lake build`: incremental green throughout every commit; final full `lake build LerayHopf`

body:
Enabling the documented hook (`git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks`) on macOS makes every push fail:

```
scripts/hooks/pre-push: line 43: flock: command not found
```

`flock(1)` is a util-linux tool and does not exist on darwin. Options: fall back to a mkdir-based lock or `shlock` when `flock` is absent, or skip serialization on darwin with a warning (single-user laptop ≠ the 3.42GiB-cgroup shared host the serialization protects).

Until fixed, macOS contributors must leave `core.hooksPath` unset and run `./scripts/agent-preflight.sh` manually before pushing (which is what the orchestrator is doing for the #110–#114 refactor wave).

body:
## Purpose

Final pre-publication review of the codebase from two angles the formalization campaigns never optimized for: (i) **readability as mathematics** — does the Lean development decompose the way a natural-language proof does, or did tool-scarcity-driven brute force leave monoliths? — and (ii) **reusability** — are the function-space / inequality layers generic enough to serve a broader PDE-formalization library (pdelib), or over-fitted to Leray–Hopf? This issue records the verdict, the priority framework, and the roadmap; the concrete work is tracked in the sub-issues below. **No refactoring is executed under this issue itself.**

Method: four independent read-only audits over the full `LerayHopf/` tree (~42.7k lines, ~80 files) — toolkit-generality, R3/Torus duplication, monolith decomposability, and outsider-view architecture — with load-bearing claims spot-verified against source.

## Verdict: publish first — after fixing the names

**Nothing found blocks publication mathematically.** Specifically:

- No audited duplication or monolith makes any *statement* wrong; where the two lanes differ, they differ by domain-appropriate hypotheses, not silently weakened content.
- The feared "agentic brute force" signature (blind tactic-spam) is largely absent; 49 `maxHeartbeats` bumps repo-wide cluster on a handful of genuinely heavy proofs. The real debt is proof-body granularity and copy-paste, both repairable post-release.
- Positive findings an external reviewer will notice: the import DAG has **zero dead files**, doc-string coverage on public API is high, and all 5 remaining `sorry`s are `ALLOW_SORRY`-marked scaffolds or tracked walls.

The priority framework is **irreversibility**: in Lean, the public API is exactly *declaration names + module paths*. Once external work pins them, renames become permanently breaking. Everything else — deduplication, abstraction, proof-splitting — is internal and can be done safely at leisure after release. Therefore the pre-release gate is deliberately small and purely nominal:

## Pre-release gate (recommended blocking, ~3 mechanical PRs)

- [x] #108 — retire the stale `Axiomatic` vocabulary (capstone theorem names `exists_lerayHopf_{torus3,r3}_axiomatic`, the four `*Axiomatic*`/`AxiomaticClosure` files). The project's headline claim is *axiom-free*; its two headline identifiers say the opposite. Cheap now, breaking forever after. (Reverses #1 finding 3, which introduced the suffix when it was still true.)
- [x] #109 — move the 𝕋³ lane under `LerayHopf/Torus/` (module paths are API; the flat `Torus*.lean` + torus-only-but-generically-named root files are the one layout decision that gets costlier every day after release). Land before #108's file renames.
- [x] #110 — de-stale release-facing docs (`HANDOFF.md` claims 1 axiom/lane; `docs/formalization-review-ja.md` cites nonexistent names; root `LerayHopf.lean` docstring still describes the 5-file MVP).

Together with #106 (LICENSE/CITATION), these close the release checklist. No other item below should delay publication; there is no external deadline, but priority-securing argues against letting internal polish gate the public result.

## Post-release roadmap (priority order)

- [x] #111 — **dedup, mechanical** (~2,300–2,900 near-duplicate lines, ~6–7% of repo): tensor/edge-gluing layer duplicated near-verbatim across lanes (72 identical declaration names, verified), Plancherel-kernel quartet ×3, `private`-visibility "local copy" lemmas, one twice-built BLT tower. Five bounded PRs; only one needs re-proving.
- [x] #113 — **pdelib staging**: decouple pure-analysis modules from the Galerkin/NS import chain (currently, importing the Rellich embedding drags in the whole solution-package apparatus), extract ~1,500 lines of misfiled generic infrastructure out of `EnergyClassConvection.lean` and friends, harden the `GelfandTriple`/`DissipativeEvolution` interfaces (#1 finding 1, closing its two `ALLOW_SORRY`s), cheap `Fin 3 → Fin n` signature generalizations, and a `docs/pdelib-staging.md` inventory. The generality audit's good news: `Bochner/` is already abstract Mathlib-style work filling real mathlib gaps (Lions–Magenes apparatus, sequential Banach–Alaoglu, Fréchet–Kolmogorov); `TensorIntersection.lean` and `EvolutionTriple.lean` are lift-ready almost verbatim.
- [x] #112 — **Galerkin abstraction** (architect-gated campaign): a `GalerkinDomain` interface + generic finite-dim Galerkin-ODE layer, making both lanes instances of one parametric development. Highest leverage, highest blast radius (both `AxiomaticClosure` interface files sit at the base of their lane's DAG) — exactly why it must not be rushed pre-release. Follows #111.
- [x] #114 — **proof-granularity / NL correspondence** (rolling, low-tier): split the 150–350-line have-chain monoliths into named textbook-step lemmas (largest: three proofs in the 3,455-line `AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean`), add the missing `b(u,v,v)=0` corollary. Directly feeds the proof-notes UI (lean-pde-notes#1) — one named lemma per annotatable textbook step.

Dependency notes: #109 → #108 (move once, then rename). #111 PR-3 shrinks #112's surface. #113 PR-2 shares module layout with #111 PR-2. #114 must not touch files in flight under #111/#113 (one writer per file).

## Relationship to #1

#1 (2026-06-24 architecture audit) remains open; its findings 2 and 4 were since implemented (Core/axiomatic import split; axiom-leakage CI gate), finding 3 is *reversed* by #108 (the axiom-zero flip inverted its premise), and findings 1 and 5 are absorbed into #113 (interface hardening; total-`tsum` domain-control APIs). Suggest closing #1 with a pointer here once #113 lands, or re-scoping it to finding 5 alone.

body:
## Context

Post-release refactor (see umbrella issue), lowest urgency, incremental by design. The monolith audit's headline: the feared "blind tactic-spam" is largely absent — files already carry step/tier narration (`/-! ### Step … -/`), doc-strings are strong, and `maxHeartbeats` bumps (49 repo-wide) cluster exactly on a handful of genuinely heavy proofs. The real gap is **proof-body granularity**: a dozen 150–350-line proofs each perform 3–5 distinct textbook steps inside one unnamed `have`-chain. Splitting them into named lemmas is what makes the Lean development *cite-able step-by-step against a natural-language proof* — directly feeding the proof-notes UI (Japanese-annotated interactive notes, lean-pde-notes#1), where a named lemma per textbook step is the unit of annotation.

## Targets (from the audit; line spans on `main` @ 013c4a0)

**Tier 1 — the limit-passage monsters (`R3/AubinLionsLimitPassage.lean`, 3,455 lines, 86 decls):**
- `weakFormNS_limit_passage` (~335 lines, 3008–3342), `bForm_limit_convection_bound` (~224, 2784–3007), `weakFormNS_galerkinTest_limit` (~169, 2551–2719). All three repeat the same measure/sup-bound boilerplate — extract a shared `RestrictAvgIntegralBridge` helper, then split each along its internal integrability / difference-bound / vanishing-squeeze structure (closes over local context, so extraction requires generalizing to explicit arguments — light re-proving, no new math).
- File split: `SteklovAverages.lean` (1484–2335, self-contained) and `ViscousWeakLsc.lean` (548–1483) are mechanical extractions; fix the stale section header over 845–1483 while at it.
- Note: the file split changes module paths — post-release this needs the old module to keep re-exporting (`import` shim) or a deprecation note; decide per PR.

**Tier 2 — named-lemma extraction in place (no file moves):**
- `TorusTraceEnergy.lean`: `energy_ineq_of_representative` (~209 lines), `exists_weak_representative` (~151) — linear have-chains; split into viscous-l.s.c. / Fatou / assembly lemmas.
- `R3/SobolevEmbedding.lean`: `schwartz_h1_gradConv_aux` (~194), `gns_L6_of_memH1_R3` (~175) — split along their already-commented step boundaries (naming only).
- `R3/EnergyClassConvection.lean`: the two ~190-line Schwartz-approximation/weak-Leibniz proofs deserve citable names ("density lemma" per the textbook narrative).
- `R3/GalerkinTrilinearBound.lean`: name the (3,2,6)-Hölder splitting capstone that is currently 6 unnamed private helpers.

**Tier 3 — small correctness-of-narrative items:**

- `R3/FrechetKolmogorov.lean`: reorder so FK steps 1–4 appear in textbook order (step 2 currently precedes step 1).

## Plan

Rolling series of small PRs (one file or one proof-cluster each), any order after Tier 3 (do Tier 3 first — one afternoon, immediate payoff). Each PR: extract named lemmas with doc-strings phrased as the textbook step they implement; no statement changes to existing public theorems; deleted `maxHeartbeats` bumps where splitting removes the pressure (expected but not required).

## Orchestration

No orchestration needed; this is ideal background work for a single mid-tier (`sonnet`) `lean-prover` per PR under the standard harness, `pr-reviewer` gate. Good candidate for a slow umbrella-loop lane if one is running. Coordinate with #R4/#R6 only to avoid touching the same files in flight (one writer per file).

## Acceptance criteria

- No single proof > ~150 lines in the touched files (soft target; justified exceptions documented).
- Every extracted lemma's doc-string names its textbook step; the proof-notes corpus can reference them.
